profile.summary: Strong comic writing and sharp institutional satire; emotionally rewarding journeys and friendships; gripping fictional mystery with satisfying narrative stakes; highly original premises are welcome but not sufficient; enjoys deep psychological atmosphere and strong character work. Mood changes greatly each evening; exclude true crime. Likes, alright and loved ratings are separate signals; did not finish or stopped is not the same as disliked.

film-fantastic-mr-fox.note: Expected to love it based on hype and how much I enjoyed the French dispatch

tv-midnight-mass.note: The mystery and horror were not engaging enough.

tv-superstore.note: Hated it; jokes did not land.

tv-what-we-do-in-the-shadows.note: Didn't enjoy it despite loving The Office US.

tv-hawkeye.note: Disliked the Marvel series featuring the young archer.

tv-bojack-horseman.note: Started, never finished. Exact season and episode unknown.

tv-detectorists.note: Tried it but couldn't get into it.

tv-slow-horses.note: Started, never finished. Exact season and episode unknown.

tv-fargo.note: Season 1 watched; wasn't interested enough to watch more.

film-the-french-dispatch.note: Mentioned enjoying it in the Fantastic Mr. Fox comment; no formal rating supplied.

catalogue.title: Adaptation.
catalogue.synopsis: A blocked screenwriter struggles to adapt a book and becomes entangled in his own screenplay.
catalogue.why: Kaufman's self-referential weirdness could land between the invention of Eternal Sunshine and the chaos of Frank.

catalogue.title: Palm Springs
catalogue.synopsis: Two wedding guests become trapped reliving the same day, with increasingly complicated feelings.
catalogue.why: A genuinely funny high-concept romance: absurdity, commitment and surprising tenderness in one tidy film.

catalogue.title: Hot Rod
catalogue.synopsis: An inept would-be stuntman attempts a spectacular jump to raise money for his stepfather.
catalogue.why: Its gleeful stupidity and commitment to bizarre bits could hit your Step Brothers and I Think You Should Leave sweet spot.

catalogue.title: The Nice Guys
catalogue.synopsis: A hapless private investigator and a bruiser investigate a missing woman in 1970s Los Angeles.
catalogue.why: Idiotic men, terrific comic timing and an actual mystery: the balance you say matters.

catalogue.title: Arrival
catalogue.synopsis: A linguist joins an effort to communicate with mysterious spacecraft that have appeared worldwide.
catalogue.why: An emotionally potent puzzle-box story with intelligence and restraint, especially promising after Severance and Eternal Sunshine.

catalogue.title: Swiss Army Man
catalogue.synopsis: A stranded man befriends a corpse whose impossible abilities lead them on an unlikely journey.
catalogue.why: Its deeply odd mix of vulnerability and absurdity makes it an adventurous next step after Frank.

catalogue.title: Little Miss Sunshine
catalogue.synopsis: An eccentric family drives a failing van across America for their daughter's beauty pageant.
catalogue.why: You respond to messy people, sharp laughs and earned warmth; this combines all three.

catalogue.title: Being John Malkovich
catalogue.synopsis: A puppeteer discovers a portal allowing visitors to inhabit an actor's mind for fifteen minutes.
catalogue.why: Your positive rating confirms a taste for bold identity-bending premises, even without an emotional home run.

catalogue.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling laundromat owner is swept into a multiverse crisis involving alternate versions of her life.
catalogue.why: A confirmed favourite: huge imagination, ferocious silliness and a moving emotional core.

catalogue.title: The Lobster
catalogue.synopsis: Single adults at a remote hotel face an absurd deadline to find love or become animals.
catalogue.why: Your liking for its discomfort suggests risk-taking is welcome, though cold surrealism alone isn't enough.

catalogue.title: Her
catalogue.synopsis: A lonely writer develops a relationship with a sophisticated artificial intelligence voice.
catalogue.why: Your positive response points to thoughtful technology stories grounded in human longing.

catalogue.title: In Bruges
catalogue.synopsis: Two hitmen hide in a Belgian town as guilt, boredom and a botched job catch up with them.
catalogue.why: A confirmed favourite and almost a template for your taste in savage humour with unexpected heart.

catalogue.title: Parasite
catalogue.synopsis: An impoverished family infiltrates a wealthy household through increasingly elaborate deceptions.
catalogue.why: Your love for its razor-sharp storytelling confirms social satire and suspense make a powerful combination.

catalogue.title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
catalogue.synopsis: A daydreaming photo editor finally ventures into the world to find a missing photograph.
catalogue.why: Your love of its wonder and movement is a crucial counterweight to the darker side of your taste.

catalogue.title: Get Out
catalogue.synopsis: A young man visits his girlfriend's family and uncovers disturbing secrets behind their hospitality.
catalogue.why: You liked its socially charged mystery; a good sign for idea-driven horror with real narrative payoff.

catalogue.title: Whiplash
catalogue.synopsis: An ambitious young drummer enters a brutal contest of wills with his demanding teacher.
catalogue.why: Your positive rating supports intense character battles, although intensity itself doesn't guarantee love.

catalogue.title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
catalogue.synopsis: Former lovers undergo a procedure to erase each other, only for memories to resist oblivion.
catalogue.why: One of your favourites and a key anchor for strange premises with an enormous emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: Into the Wild
catalogue.synopsis: A young graduate abandons convention to travel across America and live on his own terms.
catalogue.why: Your affection for searching, aspirational journeys makes this a defining part of your profile.

catalogue.title: Frank
catalogue.synopsis: A novice musician joins an eccentric experimental band led by an enigmatic man in an oversized head.
catalogue.why: Its offbeat humour and sympathetic oddness neatly encapsulate what you value in unconventional cinema.

catalogue.title: Wild Tales
catalogue.synopsis: Six darkly comic stories show ordinary people reaching spectacular breaking points.
catalogue.why: Your enthusiasm for beautifully escalating bad behaviour makes this another foundational reference.

catalogue.title: Forrest Gump
catalogue.synopsis: A kindhearted man drifts through decades of American history while searching for connection.
catalogue.why: A favourite that proves heartfelt, accessible storytelling belongs alongside your art-house interests.

catalogue.title: Step Brothers
catalogue.synopsis: Two immature grown men become unwilling housemates when their single parents marry.
catalogue.why: Your affection for unapologetically stupid comedy means serious recommendations must never crowd this out.

catalogue.title: Wedding Crashers
catalogue.synopsis: Two friends attend strangers' weddings to meet women until one falls into an inconvenient romance.
catalogue.why: A useful anchor for mainstream, high-energy, personality-led comedy.

catalogue.title: The Hangover
catalogue.synopsis: Friends wake from a Las Vegas bachelor party with no memory and a missing groom.
catalogue.why: You enjoy chaotic ensemble comedy where ridiculous events keep escalating.

catalogue.title: The Truman Show
catalogue.synopsis: A genial insurance salesman starts suspecting his entire life is an elaborate television production.
catalogue.why: Jim Carrey, an inspired existential hook and real feeling make this especially central to your tastes.

catalogue.title: The Mask
catalogue.synopsis: A timid bank clerk transforms into a manic cartoon-like trickster whenever he wears a mysterious mask.
catalogue.why: Carrey's full-throttle physical comedy fits the flamboyantly absurd side of your viewing habits.

catalogue.title: Liar Liar
catalogue.synopsis: A lawyer is magically forced to tell the truth for a day when he desperately needs to lie.
catalogue.why: A classic Carrey showcase of escalating farce and immaculate comic commitment.

catalogue.title: Bruce Almighty
catalogue.synopsis: A frustrated television reporter is temporarily granted divine powers to prove he could run things better.
catalogue.why: A big-hearted high-concept comedy combining Jim Carrey's manic energy with an emotional finish.

catalogue.title: Man on the Moon
catalogue.synopsis: Jim Carrey portrays Andy Kaufman, a performer who challenged the boundaries between comedy and provocation.
catalogue.why: Its obsession with uncomfortable performance seems made for someone who loves both Carrey and I Think You Should Leave.

catalogue.title: The Cable Guy
catalogue.synopsis: An awkward friendship with a cable installer turns into an increasingly unsettling obsession.
catalogue.why: Carrey's disturbing comic persona could appeal to your taste for uncomfortable humour.

catalogue.title: I Love You Phillip Morris
catalogue.synopsis: A charming con artist becomes determined to reunite with the man he loves through outrageous schemes.
catalogue.why: Carrey in a genuinely odd, tender and morally questionable story is a particularly promising combination.

catalogue.title: Dumb and Dumber
catalogue.synopsis: Two spectacularly foolish friends take a cross-country trip to return a suitcase to its owner.
catalogue.why: A benchmark of broad comedy whose commitment to idiocy aligns with your Step Brothers affection.

catalogue.title: The Big Lebowski
catalogue.synopsis: A laid-back slacker is mistaken for a millionaire and pulled into an increasingly confusing kidnapping plot.
catalogue.why: Quotable eccentric characters and shaggy absurdity should suit your appetite for comic personality.

catalogue.title: Burn After Reading
catalogue.synopsis: A misplaced intelligence memoir collides with a set of vain, foolish Washington residents.
catalogue.why: Almost everyone behaves terribly and the plotting turns their incompetence into savage farce.

catalogue.title: Seven Psychopaths
catalogue.synopsis: A screenwriter and his volatile friends become entangled in the theft of a gangster's beloved dog.
catalogue.why: Martin McDonagh's dark jokes and spiralling mess make it a logical step from In Bruges.

catalogue.title: The Banshees of Inisherin
catalogue.synopsis: A friendship on a remote Irish island ends abruptly and escalates into stubborn mutual cruelty.
catalogue.why: A darker, more contemplative McDonagh film that tests your love for humour mixed with painful emotion.

catalogue.title: The Death of Stalin
catalogue.synopsis: Soviet officials turn on one another after Stalin dies, scrambling for survival and power.
catalogue.why: The savage political farce and awful personalities should resonate after Succession and Sunny.

catalogue.title: Four Lions
catalogue.synopsis: A group of inept would-be terrorists stumble through increasingly disastrous plans.
catalogue.why: Very black British satire whose commitment to stupidity could match your taste for brutal comedy.

catalogue.title: The Menu
catalogue.synopsis: Guests at an exclusive island restaurant discover their tasting menu comes with sinister intentions.
catalogue.why: Controlled social satire, escalating menace and strong narrative hooks follow naturally from Parasite.

catalogue.title: Triangle of Sadness
catalogue.synopsis: Models and billionaires aboard a luxury yacht find social hierarchies overturned by disaster.
catalogue.why: A vicious class satire that may appeal if Parasite's power games were what hooked you.

catalogue.title: The Favourite
catalogue.synopsis: Rival courtiers vie for influence over an ill queen in an extravagant royal household.
catalogue.why: Scheming, nastiness and sharply comic power struggles have clear Succession appeal.

catalogue.title: Poor Things
catalogue.synopsis: A revived young woman embarks on an uninhibited journey of discovery across an eccentric world.
catalogue.why: Bold visual originality and anarchic humour could delight you; its deliberate excess may be divisive.

catalogue.title: Kinds of Kindness
catalogue.synopsis: Three unsettling stories explore control, devotion and desperate attempts to remake relationships.
catalogue.why: A deliberately difficult, surreal experiment that tests how much uncomfortable oddness you want.

catalogue.title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
catalogue.synopsis: A fastidious concierge and his lobby boy become embroiled in a stolen painting and an inheritance dispute.
catalogue.why: Its immaculate comic universe and eccentric personalities offer a very different flavour of distinctive filmmaking.

catalogue.title: The Royal Tenenbaums
catalogue.synopsis: The estranged members of a once-promising family reconvene around their manipulative patriarch.
catalogue.why: Flawed people, precise humour and poignancy make it a strong character-led essential.

catalogue.title: Jojo Rabbit
catalogue.synopsis: A lonely German boy in wartime confronts his prejudices with help from his imaginary friend.
catalogue.why: A risky balance of absurd humour and heartbreaking sentiment is right in your cross-genre sweet spot.

catalogue.title: Hunt for the Wilderpeople
catalogue.synopsis: A foster boy and his reluctant guardian become fugitives in the New Zealand wilderness.
catalogue.why: Adventure, lovable oddballs and earned feeling should appeal to the Walter Mitty side of you.

catalogue.title: What We Do in the Shadows
catalogue.synopsis: Flat-sharing vampires try to navigate modern life in a faux documentary of domestic disasters.
catalogue.why: You disliked the series, so this is a cautious curiosity rather than a strong match; the film's tighter format may differ.

catalogue.title: Popstar: Never Stop Never Stopping
catalogue.synopsis: A clueless pop megastar confronts career collapse and a spectacularly misjudged solo tour.
catalogue.why: Packed with deliberately stupid jokes and musical absurdity from the Hot Rod team.

catalogue.title: Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story
catalogue.synopsis: A fictional musical legend barrels through the clichés of a rock-and-roll biopic.
catalogue.why: Relentlessly silly parody with jokes coming from every direction rather than a complex plot.

catalogue.title: MacGruber
catalogue.synopsis: A disgraced special-operations agent returns for one disastrously incompetent mission.
catalogue.why: A divisive commitment-to-the-bit comedy that could play very well with your absurdist streak.

catalogue.title: Game Night
catalogue.synopsis: Friends hosting a murder-mystery party discover their carefully planned game is not what it seems.
catalogue.why: A genuinely funny mainstream comedy with an actual unfolding mystery and escalating errors.

catalogue.title: 21 Jump Street
catalogue.synopsis: Two rookie officers pose as high-school students to infiltrate a drug ring.
catalogue.why: Fast, self-aware comedy whose stupid situations are backed by sharp joke-writing.

catalogue.title: 22 Jump Street
catalogue.synopsis: The undercover partners return to education, this time to investigate suspicious activity at college.
catalogue.why: A very self-aware sequel that turns familiar comedy mechanics into running jokes.

catalogue.title: The Other Guys
catalogue.synopsis: Two overlooked police officers attempt to prove themselves on a financial-crime case.
catalogue.why: Will Ferrell chaos paired with a ridiculous buddy-cop plot should interest a Step Brothers fan.

catalogue.title: Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby
catalogue.synopsis: A NASCAR superstar is forced to rethink everything after a flashy rival steals his spotlight.
catalogue.why: Broad, quotable Will Ferrell comedy with precisely the sort of total commitment you enjoy.

catalogue.title: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
catalogue.synopsis: An arrogant 1970s newsreader struggles when an ambitious woman joins his newsroom.
catalogue.why: A major touchstone of absurd ensemble comedy and performative male stupidity.

catalogue.title: Superbad
catalogue.synopsis: Two teenage friends plan one legendary party before leaving for separate colleges.
catalogue.why: Wildly quotable chaos gives way to a surprisingly sincere friendship story.

catalogue.title: Booksmart
catalogue.synopsis: Two academic overachievers decide to cram four years of missed partying into one night.
catalogue.why: A lively, modern coming-of-age comedy with both big laughs and real affection.

catalogue.title: Bridesmaids
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling woman clashes with a wealthy rival while helping organise her best friend's wedding.
catalogue.why: Escalating disasters, brutally awkward situations and standout comic performances.

catalogue.title: The 40-Year-Old Virgin
catalogue.synopsis: A sheltered electronics-store employee receives disastrously enthusiastic dating advice from his colleagues.
catalogue.why: A broad comedy that also takes its central relationships seriously.

catalogue.title: I Love You, Man
catalogue.synopsis: An engaged man tries to find a best friend before his wedding.
catalogue.why: Awkward male friendship and quotable nonsense make it a relaxed evening option.

catalogue.title: Forgetting Sarah Marshall
catalogue.synopsis: A musician retreats to Hawaii after a breakup, only to run into his ex and her new partner.
catalogue.why: A proper romantic-comedy story with ridiculous supporting characters and a good emotional centre.

catalogue.title: The Darjeeling Limited
catalogue.synopsis: Three estranged brothers reunite for a train journey through India while processing grief.
catalogue.why: An eccentric travel-and-family film that could appeal to your searching adventure tastes.

catalogue.title: Almost Famous
catalogue.synopsis: A teenage journalist joins a rock band's tour and discovers the complicated lives behind the music.
catalogue.why: Joyful immersion in a different world, with wistfulness and memorable characters.

catalogue.title: The Way Way Back
catalogue.synopsis: A shy teenager finds unlikely friendship and confidence while working at a water park.
catalogue.why: A warm, funny coming-of-age film for the Shrinking and Walter Mitty side of your taste.

catalogue.title: The Fundamentals of Caring
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving caregiver takes a sarcastic teenager on a road trip full of unexpected encounters.
catalogue.why: Funny dialogue and gradually earned affection in a manageable road-trip story.

catalogue.title: Captain Fantastic
catalogue.synopsis: A father raising his children off-grid must bring them into conventional society for a family crisis.
catalogue.why: Shares Into the Wild's questioning of normal life while adding emotionally charged family conflict.

catalogue.title: The Peanut Butter Falcon
catalogue.synopsis: A young man escapes his care home to pursue wrestling dreams alongside an unlikely companion.
catalogue.why: Gentle oddball adventure with a genuinely warm emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: The Holdovers
catalogue.synopsis: A cantankerous teacher supervises students stranded at boarding school over Christmas.
catalogue.why: Bitterly funny, flawed people slowly reveal their better sides; a promising Ted Lasso-adjacent mood.

catalogue.title: Good Will Hunting
catalogue.synopsis: An exceptionally gifted but troubled young janitor forms an unlikely bond with a therapist.
catalogue.why: Character writing and earned vulnerability make it a must-consider emotional essential.

catalogue.title: Dead Poets Society
catalogue.synopsis: A charismatic teacher inspires students at a restrictive boarding school to think for themselves.
catalogue.why: Its passionate approach to life and moving friendships suits your aspirational film favourites.

catalogue.title: About Time
catalogue.synopsis: A young man discovers he can revisit moments in his life and attempts to build the perfect relationship.
catalogue.why: A charming time-travel premise mainly used to explore ordinary love and the passing of time.

catalogue.title: The Big Sick
catalogue.synopsis: A comedian's new relationship faces cultural differences and an unexpected medical crisis.
catalogue.why: Natural humour, flawed people and a genuine emotional arc rather than sugary sentiment.

catalogue.title: 500 Days of Summer
catalogue.synopsis: A nonlinear account of a relationship asks what happens when expectation and reality collide.
catalogue.why: Playful structure and bittersweet feelings bring Eternal Sunshine to mind without repeating it.

catalogue.title: The Worst Person in the World
catalogue.synopsis: A young woman in Oslo navigates career indecision, romance and the fear of choosing a life.
catalogue.why: Funny, surprising and deeply human; a strong bridge from Normal People and Eternal Sunshine.

catalogue.title: Past Lives
catalogue.synopsis: Two childhood friends separated by migration reflect on the lives they might have shared.
catalogue.why: Quiet emotional depth and alternate-life longing echo parts of your Eternal Sunshine preference.

catalogue.title: Aftersun
catalogue.synopsis: A woman revisits memories of a childhood holiday with her father, reinterpreting what she saw.
catalogue.why: A powerful, understated emotional film if you want something that stays with you.

catalogue.title: Manchester by the Sea
catalogue.synopsis: A withdrawn man returns to his hometown when a family death forces him to face old wounds.
catalogue.why: A devastating character study for evenings when you actively want heavy emotional storytelling.

catalogue.title: The Pursuit of Happyness
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling salesman cares for his son while chasing an almost impossible career breakthrough.
catalogue.why: Resilience, hope and accessible big feelings link to Forrest Gump and Walter Mitty.

catalogue.title: The Intouchables
catalogue.synopsis: An unlikely friendship develops between a wealthy disabled man and his unconventional carer.
catalogue.why: Natural comic chemistry with generous emotion, well aligned with your Shrinking and Ted Lasso appreciation.

catalogue.title: Amélie
catalogue.synopsis: A shy Parisian woman quietly engineers small pleasures in the lives of the people around her.
catalogue.why: Whimsical storytelling and enormous visual personality could satisfy your softer inventive-film tastes.

catalogue.title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
catalogue.synopsis: A washed-up ocean explorer launches a bizarre revenge expedition with his eccentric crew.
catalogue.why: Absurd personalities and extravagant adventuring, though the dry humour is a matter of taste.

catalogue.title: The Straight Story
catalogue.synopsis: An elderly man travels hundreds of miles by lawn mower to reconnect with his estranged brother.
catalogue.why: A remarkably gentle, unusual journey film that tests your enthusiasm for humanity over spectacle.

catalogue.title: Nomadland
catalogue.synopsis: A woman joins a community of American van-dwellers after losing her job and home.
catalogue.why: Quiet freedom and American landscapes could connect with Into the Wild, if the contemplative pace suits you.

catalogue.title: The Motorcycle Diaries
catalogue.synopsis: Two friends travel across South America and experience encounters that change their worldview.
catalogue.why: A youthful, restless journey with genuine political and emotional discovery.

catalogue.title: The Way
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving father walks the Camino de Santiago and unexpectedly finds companionship.
catalogue.why: An absorbing, human travel narrative for your love of life-changing journeys.

catalogue.title: The Martian
catalogue.synopsis: An astronaut stranded on Mars must improvise solutions while Earth races to bring him home.
catalogue.why: Problem-solving, warmth and humour embedded in a cracking high-stakes sci-fi adventure.

catalogue.title: Interstellar
catalogue.synopsis: Explorers venture beyond the solar system searching for a future home for humanity.
catalogue.why: High-concept spectacle grounded in love and sacrifice is a particularly strong theoretical match.

catalogue.title: Inception
catalogue.synopsis: A professional thief enters layered dreams to plant an idea in a target's subconscious.
catalogue.why: An engrossing puzzle engine with strong momentum for your Severance-and-Loki brain.

catalogue.title: Memento
catalogue.synopsis: A man unable to form new memories follows clues to investigate his wife's murder.
catalogue.why: Its ingenious structure and central mystery should feed your appetite for active interpretation.

catalogue.title: The Prestige
catalogue.synopsis: Two Victorian magicians become obsessed with outdoing each other at devastating personal cost.
catalogue.why: Rivalry, obsession and intricate reveals combine the qualities you enjoy in Succession and Severance.

catalogue.title: Ex Machina
catalogue.synopsis: A programmer is invited to test an experimental android at an isolated research facility.
catalogue.why: Intimate AI-driven intrigue with mounting psychological tension and strong ideas.

catalogue.title: Annihilation
catalogue.synopsis: A biologist joins an expedition into a mysterious ecological zone where nature behaves unnaturally.
catalogue.why: Striking originality and a deeply unsettling puzzle should suit your darker speculative taste.

catalogue.title: Coherence
catalogue.synopsis: A dinner party becomes frighteningly unstable as a comet passes overhead.
catalogue.why: A lean, mind-bending concept with little wasted motion and plenty to discuss afterwards.

catalogue.title: Predestination
catalogue.synopsis: A temporal agent pursues an elusive bomber through a labyrinth of identity and fate.
catalogue.why: If intricate narrative puzzles are tonight's goal, this is an unusually committed example.

catalogue.title: Source Code
catalogue.synopsis: A soldier relives the final minutes before a commuter train explosion to identify its cause.
catalogue.why: High-concept mystery told at a propulsive pace rather than requiring a season-long commitment.

catalogue.title: Looper
catalogue.synopsis: A contract killer is ordered to eliminate a target who turns out to be his future self.
catalogue.why: A satisfying sci-fi hook backed by an increasingly personal moral conflict.

catalogue.title: Moon
catalogue.synopsis: A solitary worker on a lunar outpost begins questioning his circumstances near the end of his contract.
catalogue.why: An intimate identity mystery that should appeal to your interest in human consequences of speculative ideas.

catalogue.title: Blade Runner
catalogue.synopsis: A detective hunts synthetic humans in a rain-soaked future city and begins questioning their humanity.
catalogue.why: A foundational atmospheric identity puzzle whose influence runs through so much of your favourite science fiction.

catalogue.title: Blade Runner 2049
catalogue.synopsis: A new replicant hunter discovers a secret capable of changing the future of his society.
catalogue.why: Stunning worldbuilding and philosophical mystery, though its patient pace is a meaningful caveat.

catalogue.title: Children of Men
catalogue.synopsis: In a future where humanity has become infertile, a disillusioned man protects a miraculous young woman.
catalogue.why: Immersive, urgent speculative fiction with genuine emotional and political stakes.

catalogue.title: District 9
catalogue.synopsis: An official handling alien refugees in Johannesburg becomes caught in a violent transformation.
catalogue.why: Social satire, strong premise and messy human behaviour combine to make the action mean something.

catalogue.title: Edge of Tomorrow
catalogue.synopsis: A soldier repeatedly relives a disastrous alien battle and gradually learns how to survive.
catalogue.why: Fast, clever and surprisingly funny high-concept entertainment with an addictive loop.

catalogue.title: Minority Report
catalogue.synopsis: A future police officer accused of a crime not yet committed tries to prove his innocence.
catalogue.why: A sophisticated moral premise delivered as an engaging, full-blooded thriller.

catalogue.title: Donnie Darko
catalogue.synopsis: A troubled teenager encounters a disturbing rabbit figure who foretells the end of the world.
catalogue.why: Cult mystery, suburban unease and emotional oddness give it clear high-concept appeal.

catalogue.title: The Matrix
catalogue.synopsis: A computer hacker discovers the world he inhabits may be an elaborate manufactured illusion.
catalogue.why: Essential idea-driven blockbuster filmmaking, with a story every bit as important as the spectacle.

catalogue.title: Dark City
catalogue.synopsis: An amnesiac wakes in a city where reality seems to change every night.
catalogue.why: Noir atmosphere, identity confusion and ingenious worldbuilding should reward your curiosity.

catalogue.title: The Science of Sleep
catalogue.synopsis: An imaginative man blurs dream and waking life while falling for his neighbour.
catalogue.why: Gondry's handmade surrealism could tempt you, though its story is less tightly resolved.

catalogue.title: The Fall
catalogue.synopsis: An injured stuntman tells a young girl an extravagant story that begins to mirror his despair.
catalogue.why: Extraordinary visual imagination and moving storytelling align with your fascination for imaginative escape.

catalogue.title: Big Fish
catalogue.synopsis: A son attempts to understand his estranged father through fantastical stories of his life.
catalogue.why: Whimsical invention with a significant emotional payoff may be your Forrest Gump and Eternal Sunshine overlap.

catalogue.title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
catalogue.synopsis: A man born with an elderly body experiences time and relationships in reverse.
catalogue.why: An expansive life story focused on mortality and love, though its tempo is leisurely.

catalogue.title: The Green Mile
catalogue.synopsis: A prison guard encounters an extraordinary inmate on death row in Depression-era America.
catalogue.why: A powerful mainstream emotional story with mystery and the kind of heartfelt scope you appreciate.

catalogue.title: The Shawshank Redemption
catalogue.synopsis: A wrongly convicted banker quietly builds hope and friendships over decades in prison.
catalogue.why: A compelling, deeply satisfying human story and one of the clearest essentials regardless of taste.

catalogue.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
catalogue.synopsis: A rebellious new patient clashes with a controlling nurse in a psychiatric institution.
catalogue.why: Fascinating personalities and an unforgettable battle over control and autonomy.

catalogue.title: 12 Angry Men
catalogue.synopsis: A jury debates one murder trial as doubt and personal prejudice unravel apparent certainty.
catalogue.why: A demonstration that clever writing and character conflict can make a single room riveting.

catalogue.title: The Social Network
catalogue.synopsis: A Harvard student's social website sparks personal betrayal and a series of legal battles.
catalogue.why: Razor-sharp dialogue and vicious ambition offer a feature-film counterpart to Succession.

catalogue.title: The Wolf of Wall Street
catalogue.synopsis: A charismatic stockbroker constructs an empire of financial fraud and obscene excess.
catalogue.why: Terrible people, outrageous comedy and propulsive storytelling fit several of your strongest signals.

catalogue.title: The Big Short
catalogue.synopsis: A few investors discover the financial system's hidden vulnerabilities before the 2008 crisis.
catalogue.why: Angry, inventive storytelling makes complex material accessible without losing its dark humour.

catalogue.title: Catch Me If You Can
catalogue.synopsis: A teenage con artist evades a determined federal agent while adopting ever bolder identities.
catalogue.why: Charm, character chemistry and an addictive ongoing chase make it effortlessly watchable.

catalogue.title: The Departed
catalogue.synopsis: A mole in the police and an undercover officer in the mob unknowingly hunt each other.
catalogue.why: Tremendous dramatic momentum and memorable, awful characters should keep you completely engaged.

catalogue.title: No Country for Old Men
catalogue.synopsis: A found suitcase of cash sparks an unforgiving pursuit across the Texas borderlands.
catalogue.why: Masterful dread and mounting consequence for your psychological-tension preferences.

catalogue.title: Fargo
catalogue.synopsis: A desperate car salesman arranges a kidnapping that spirals into gruesome incompetence.
catalogue.why: The film's tighter arc may appeal even though the anthology series did not pull you onward.

catalogue.title: Nightcrawler
catalogue.synopsis: An ambitious outsider exploits violent incidents to build a career in local television news.
catalogue.why: One remarkable morally repellent lead drives a tense, sharply satirical story.

catalogue.title: Prisoners
catalogue.synopsis: Two children vanish and their families descend into desperation as the investigation stalls.
catalogue.why: Dark fictional mystery built around escalating moral conflict and gripping uncertainty.

catalogue.title: Gone Girl
catalogue.synopsis: A woman's disappearance turns her husband and their marriage into a national spectacle.
catalogue.why: A brilliantly structured fictional mystery full of awful personalities and reversals.

catalogue.title: Shutter Island
catalogue.synopsis: A federal marshal visits an isolated psychiatric hospital to investigate a patient's disappearance.
catalogue.why: Gothic atmosphere, strong narrative intrigue and psychological uncertainty.

catalogue.title: The Sixth Sense
catalogue.synopsis: A child psychologist tries to help a frightened boy who claims to see the dead.
catalogue.why: Emotionally grounded supernatural mystery, particularly worth weighing against Hill House.

catalogue.title: The Others
catalogue.synopsis: A mother protecting her light-sensitive children begins suspecting something is wrong with their mansion.
catalogue.why: Elegant gothic dread with a compelling central mystery rather than cheap shocks.

catalogue.title: The Babadook

catalogue.synopsis: An irreverent Irish policeman teams with an FBI agent to investigate international smugglers.
catalogue.why: Brendan Gleeson's caustic comic timing makes this a natural In Bruges-adjacent pick.

catalogue.title: Calvary
catalogue.synopsis: An Irish priest receives a death threat and spends a week confronting his troubled parish.
catalogue.why: A darker, more contemplative companion to In Bruges, with sharp dialogue and moral complexity.

catalogue.title: War on Everyone
catalogue.synopsis: Two corrupt New Mexico cops indulge their worst impulses while pursuing a criminal.
catalogue.why: For your morally dubious, anarchic comedy streak; considerably cruder than In Bruges.

catalogue.title: The Trip
catalogue.synopsis: Two comedians tour northern England's restaurants while trading impressions and subtle insults.
catalogue.why: You may enjoy the personality-led banter of old Top Gear in a more contemplative setting.

catalogue.title: The Trip to Italy
catalogue.synopsis: Two comedians travel through Italy's restaurants while riffing on fame and friendship.
catalogue.why: Another chance to enjoy improvised bickering, travel and food without needing a dense plot.

catalogue.title: The Inbetweeners Movie
catalogue.synopsis: Four socially inept friends head abroad for a disastrous post-school holiday.
catalogue.why: Your love of The Hangover and outrageous British comedy makes this a useful comic touchstone.

catalogue.title: The Boat That Rocked
catalogue.synopsis: Pirate-radio DJs broadcast from a boat while the government tries to silence them.
catalogue.why: An upbeat ensemble full of colourful personalities that might suit a lighter evening.

catalogue.title: The World's End
catalogue.synopsis: Former school friends revisit an old pub crawl and discover their hometown has changed in alarming ways.
catalogue.why: Blends pub banter, ridiculous escalation and actual science-fiction plotting.

catalogue.title: Shaun of the Dead
catalogue.synopsis: A directionless Londoner tries to win back his girlfriend as a zombie outbreak spreads.
catalogue.why: A foundational British genre comedy combining proper jokes, escalating chaos and genuine heart.

catalogue.title: Hot Fuzz
catalogue.synopsis: An overachieving police officer is transferred to a suspiciously idyllic country village.
catalogue.why: Inventive joke density and an engaging mystery are an especially good combination for you.

catalogue.title: Attack the Block
catalogue.synopsis: South London teenagers defend their estate from an alien invasion.
catalogue.why: An energetic British genre crossover with sharp humour, momentum and character stakes.

catalogue.title: Sightseers
catalogue.synopsis: A couple's caravan holiday through the English countryside becomes increasingly murderous.
catalogue.why: Biting British black comedy about awful people, with a gloriously unpleasant sense of escalation.

catalogue.title: A Film with Me in It
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling actor and his friend try to conceal an unbelievable succession of accidents.
catalogue.why: The escalating catastrophe might appeal to your Wild Tales and absurdist comedy taste.

catalogue.title: Extra Ordinary
catalogue.synopsis: A shy Irish driving instructor uses supernatural abilities to stop an occult rock star.
catalogue.why: Quirky horror comedy with a surprisingly sweet centre and a ridiculous premise.

catalogue.title: Boys from County Hell
catalogue.synopsis: Irish road workers accidentally disturb something ancient while excavating a local legend.
catalogue.why: A shaggy, funny creature feature for when you want horror without losing the humour.

catalogue.title: The Young Offenders
catalogue.synopsis: Two Cork teenagers cycle off in search of a drug haul washed ashore.
catalogue.why: Fast-talking, deeply stupid characters with more heart than you might expect.

catalogue.title: The Commitments
catalogue.synopsis: A young Dubliner assembles a chaotic working-class soul band.
catalogue.why: Rowdy ensembles, ambition and abrasive warmth should hit several of your comic preferences.

catalogue.title: Waking Ned
catalogue.synopsis: Residents of an Irish village conspire to claim a dead neighbour's lottery winnings.
catalogue.why: A gently devious ensemble comedy that might surprise you on a cosy evening.

catalogue.title: In the Loop
catalogue.synopsis: British and American political operatives stumble toward a disastrous international conflict.
catalogue.why: If The Thick of It is a favourite, this spin-off's profanity and institutional incompetence are almost essential.

catalogue.title: The Personal History of David Copperfield
catalogue.synopsis: A young man navigates chaotic fortunes and eccentric companions in Victorian England.
catalogue.why: Armando Iannucci's comic rhythms with warmth and wonderfully odd characters.

catalogue.title: Alan Partridge: Alpha Papa
catalogue.synopsis: A vain local radio presenter becomes an unlikely hostage negotiator.
catalogue.why: Character embarrassment and spectacular professional incompetence, adjacent to The Office and Thick of It.

catalogue.title: Brian and Charles
catalogue.synopsis: A lonely Welsh inventor builds an eccentric robot companion who wants to see the world.
catalogue.why: An oddball friendship comedy that balances ridiculousness and surprisingly affecting emotion.

catalogue.title: Brigsby Bear
catalogue.synopsis: A sheltered man discovers his beloved childhood television series hides a shocking secret.
catalogue.why: A truly unusual yet tender story about imagination and finding community; strong Frank crossover.

catalogue.title: The Sasquatch Gang
catalogue.synopsis: Teenage amateur scientists become convinced they have discovered evidence of Bigfoot.
catalogue.why: Extremely daft outsider comedy; a potential cult find if Hot Rod-style silliness lands.

catalogue.title: Gentlemen Broncos
catalogue.synopsis: A teenage aspiring novelist discovers his bizarre science-fiction story has been stolen.
catalogue.why: Unfashionably weird, cringeworthy characters and elaborate fantasy sequences might appeal to your absurdist side.

catalogue.title: Napoleon Dynamite
catalogue.synopsis: An awkward Idaho teenager navigates school, family oddities and a class-election campaign.
catalogue.why: A genuine cult-comedy landmark to test your tolerance for dry, character-based weirdness.

catalogue.title: Nacho Libre
catalogue.synopsis: A monastery cook becomes a masked wrestler to support children in his care.
catalogue.why: Ridiculous physical comedy with an unexpectedly sweet heart, somewhere between dumb and endearing.

catalogue.title: The Foot Fist Way
catalogue.synopsis: A deluded taekwondo instructor's personal and professional life unravels.
catalogue.why: Awful-but-fascinating comic characters and brutal embarrassment, but purposefully abrasive.

catalogue.title: Observe and Report
catalogue.synopsis: A mall security guard develops an obsessive plan to become a real police officer.
catalogue.why: Much darker and more uncomfortable than standard Seth Rogen comedy; potentially your Sunny side.

catalogue.title: The Overnight
catalogue.synopsis: Two couples' dinner evening takes a bizarre turn as social boundaries dissolve.
catalogue.why: Compact, uncomfortable social comedy with strong unpredictable energy.

catalogue.title: The Little Hours
catalogue.synopsis: Medieval nuns and a gardener create an escalating scandal at a convent.
catalogue.why: A profane, deeply silly ensemble committed to its ridiculous period setting.

catalogue.title: They Came Together
catalogue.synopsis: A couple recount a romance that follows every ridiculous romantic-comedy cliché.
catalogue.why: A relentless genre parody that might land if you want absurd jokes rather than sentimentality.

catalogue.title: Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar
catalogue.synopsis: Two lifelong friends take a seaside holiday and stumble into a flamboyant villain's plot.
catalogue.why: Unashamedly surreal, cheerful nonsense; a good wildcard for your broad comedy appetite.

catalogue.title: Bottoms
catalogue.synopsis: Two unpopular schoolgirls launch a fight club with dubious romantic motives.
catalogue.why: Bold, absurd teenage comedy with the unapologetic energy you enjoy in Superbad.

catalogue.title: Theater Camp
catalogue.synopsis: Eccentric teachers scramble to save a summer drama camp after its founder falls ill.
catalogue.why: The improvised character comedy and affectionate chaos may appeal to your Office side.

catalogue.title: Hundreds of Beavers
catalogue.synopsis: A hapless applejack salesman battles an increasingly elaborate wilderness of costumed beavers.
catalogue.why: Inventive, near-silent slapstick that pushes absurd comedy to an astonishing extreme.

catalogue.title: One Cut of the Dead
catalogue.synopsis: A film crew attempts a zombie scene that goes spectacularly wrong.
catalogue.why: Stick with the setup: the structural payoff makes this an unusually satisfying genre-comedy surprise.

catalogue.title: Deadstream
catalogue.synopsis: A disgraced livestreamer tries to redeem himself by broadcasting overnight from a haunted house.
catalogue.why: Chaotic, inventive horror-comedy with the energy of a very bad online decision.

catalogue.title: The Final Girls
catalogue.synopsis: A teenager becomes trapped in an old slasher film starring her late mother.
catalogue.why: Self-aware horror mechanics with a genuinely emotional mother-daughter core.

catalogue.title: Tucker and Dale vs Evil
catalogue.synopsis: Two friendly hillbillies are mistaken for killers by a group of terrified students.
catalogue.why: A ridiculously escalating misunderstanding, perfect for black-comedy nights.

catalogue.title: The Babysitter
catalogue.synopsis: A boy discovers his seemingly wonderful babysitter leads a murderous cult.
catalogue.why: Bright, ridiculous horror spectacle with more jokes than psychological depth.

catalogue.title: The Frighteners
catalogue.synopsis: A psychic con artist who works with ghosts uncovers an increasingly sinister threat.
catalogue.why: Jim Carrey-era energy and imaginative supernatural mystery, with a dark streak.

catalogue.title: Death Becomes Her
catalogue.synopsis: Two bitter rivals discover the catastrophic benefits of an immortality potion.
catalogue.why: Stylish, viciously funny and deliciously macabre studio comedy.

catalogue.title: The Burbs
catalogue.synopsis: Suburban neighbours become convinced the strange family next door has a secret.
catalogue.why: Dark, silly neighbourhood paranoia with a genuinely entertaining mystery.

catalogue.title: The Money Pit
catalogue.synopsis: A couple buy a dream house that immediately begins collapsing around them.
catalogue.why: A cascade of physical disasters for your broad slapstick comedy taste.

catalogue.title: Planes, Trains and Automobiles
catalogue.synopsis: A tightly wound businessman struggles to get home with an impossibly irritating travel companion.
catalogue.why: A classic example of big laughs landing alongside a deeply satisfying emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: Uncle Buck
catalogue.synopsis: A chaotic uncle is put in charge of his brother's children during a family emergency.
catalogue.why: A sweet, messy character comedy with genuine warmth beneath the silliness.

catalogue.title: The Jerk
catalogue.synopsis: A spectacularly naive man leaves home and experiences a strange version of the American dream.
catalogue.why: A foundational absurd American comedy with a remarkably committed lead performance.

catalogue.title: Airplane!
catalogue.synopsis: A traumatised pilot must land an airliner as the entire crew falls ill.
catalogue.why: Relentless joke density and shameless stupidity: a crucial test for your comedy taste.

catalogue.title: The Naked Gun
catalogue.synopsis: A dangerously incompetent detective uncovers a plot against the Queen.
catalogue.why: Straight-faced idiocy, slapstick and non-stop visual jokes could be exactly your thing.

catalogue.title: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
catalogue.synopsis: King Arthur and his knights pursue a sacred relic across a brilliantly ridiculous medieval landscape.
catalogue.why: Surreal British comic inventiveness with a huge legacy across everything you enjoy.

catalogue.title: Monty Python's Life of Brian
catalogue.synopsis: An ordinary Judean man is repeatedly mistaken for the Messiah.
catalogue.why: Biting institutional satire and memorable absurdity in the same vein as Four Lions.

catalogue.title: The Producers
catalogue.synopsis: A crooked Broadway producer and accountant scheme to profit from a deliberately terrible musical.
catalogue.why: A landmark in outrageous satirical comedy, an important essential beyond recent favourites.

catalogue.title: Dr. Strangelove
catalogue.synopsis: Military and political leaders attempt to prevent a nuclear catastrophe caused by one general.
catalogue.why: The ultimate institutionally stupid people comedy, with historical and cinematic significance.

catalogue.title: Network
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling television network exploits the on-air breakdown of a news anchor.
catalogue.why: A furious, funny satire on media and power that connects strongly to Succession.

catalogue.title: The Apartment
catalogue.synopsis: An office worker lends his flat to executives and falls for an elevator operator.
catalogue.why: Sharp corporate satire with heartfelt romance and exceptionally elegant writing.

catalogue.title: Some Like It Hot
catalogue.synopsis: Two musicians on the run disguise themselves to join an all-women band.
catalogue.why: A timeless farce worth testing against your fondness for elaborate comic deception.

catalogue.title: The Ladykillers
catalogue.synopsis: A gang of criminals pose as musicians while lodging with an unsuspecting old woman.
catalogue.why: Classic Ealing black comedy with comic incompetence and escalating misfortune.

catalogue.title: Kind Hearts and Coronets
catalogue.synopsis: An embittered heir plots murders to advance through an aristocratic family tree.
catalogue.why: Deliciously dry, cynical British comedy that should appeal to your darker sensibility.

catalogue.title: A Fish Called Wanda
catalogue.synopsis: A jewel robbery triggers a maze of manipulation, seduction and foolishness.
catalogue.why: Big comic personalities and precise farce, right at the intersection of British and American humour.

catalogue.title: Withnail and I
catalogue.synopsis: Two unemployed actors escape London for a disastrous rural holiday.
catalogue.why: Cult British comedy built on quotable misery, indignity and brilliant character performances.

catalogue.title: The King of Comedy
catalogue.synopsis: An aspiring comedian kidnaps a famous talk-show host in pursuit of stardom.
catalogue.why: Painful delusion and social discomfort prefigure much of the comedy you already love.

catalogue.title: After Hours
catalogue.synopsis: A New Yorker experiences a nocturnal chain of increasingly surreal misfortunes.
catalogue.why: Escalating catastrophes, dark comedy and ingenious plotting make this especially promising.

catalogue.title: The Hudsucker Proxy
catalogue.synopsis: An inexperienced mailroom worker is installed as president of a corporation for cynical reasons.
catalogue.why: Stylised corporate farce and oddball invention that could suit The Big Short/Coens crossover.

catalogue.title: Raising Arizona
catalogue.synopsis: An ex-con and a police officer kidnap a baby after discovering they cannot have one.
catalogue.why: Bizarre humour, frantic energy and heartfelt absurdity wrapped in a very distinctive voice.

catalogue.title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
catalogue.synopsis: Three escaped convicts wander through Depression-era Mississippi on a mythical quest.
catalogue.why: A lively, eccentric road adventure with memorable oddballs and surprising warmth.

catalogue.title: A Serious Man
catalogue.synopsis: A physics professor's orderly life collapses under bizarre domestic and professional troubles.
catalogue.why: The Coens' bleak cosmic joke may intrigue you, though its unresolved questions are deliberately frustrating.

catalogue.title: Inside Llewyn Davis
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling folk musician drifts around 1960s New York while his career stalls.
catalogue.why: Character-rich melancholy with mordant humour, possible overlap with Frank and Inside the Wild.

catalogue.title: The Ballad of Buster Scruggs
catalogue.synopsis: Six absurd and often brutal tales unfold across the American frontier.
catalogue.why: Anthology structure, grim wit and tonal variety could appeal to your Wild Tales affection.

catalogue.title: Kiss Kiss Bang Bang
catalogue.synopsis: A petty thief posing as an actor gets dragged into a dangerous Hollywood mystery.
catalogue.why: Very witty noir plotting with an unreliable hero and fantastically quick dialogue.

catalogue.title: The Long Goodbye
catalogue.synopsis: Detective Philip Marlowe drifts into a suspicious disappearance in modern Los Angeles.
catalogue.why: A sly, eccentric noir where personality and atmosphere are as compelling as the mystery.

catalogue.title: The Last Detail
catalogue.synopsis: Two naval petty officers escort a young sailor to prison and show him a final good time.
catalogue.why: Raucous dialogue, flawed men and unexpectedly moving friendship could work very well.

catalogue.title: Harold and Maude
catalogue.synopsis: A death-obsessed young man finds an unexpected connection with a free-spirited older woman.
catalogue.why: A canonical offbeat romance balancing very black humour with life-affirming emotion.

catalogue.title: Being There
catalogue.synopsis: A sheltered gardener's naive comments are mistaken for profound political wisdom.
catalogue.why: A delicious satire of public life and institutional stupidity, though intentionally understated.

catalogue.title: The Graduate
catalogue.synopsis: A disaffected college graduate enters an ill-advised affair and develops feelings for someone else.
catalogue.why: Modern alienation, sexual awkwardness and sharp comedy make this a valuable landmark.

catalogue.title: Rushmore
catalogue.synopsis: An overly ambitious schoolboy clashes with a wealthy adult over a teacher.
catalogue.why: Eccentric flawed people and unusually exact comic character writing may land better than Fantastic Mr. Fox.

catalogue.title: Moonrise Kingdom
catalogue.synopsis: Two young outsiders run away together, drawing their island community into a search.
catalogue.why: A charming adventure with genuine yearning, possibly your Walter Mitty side of Wes Anderson.

catalogue.title: The French Dispatch
catalogue.synopsis: Stories from an eccentric American magazine unfold in a stylised French town.
catalogue.why: Already identified as something you enjoyed; included as a style reference rather than an unseen pick.

catalogue.title: Asteroid City
catalogue.synopsis: Visitors gather in a desert town where a mysterious event disrupts a youth astronomy convention.
catalogue.why: Stylised layers and emotional distance make this a real test of your Wes Anderson taste.

catalogue.title: The Life of Chuck
catalogue.synopsis: Three connected episodes work backward through one man's life amid mysterious global upheaval.
catalogue.why: A moving, unusually structured story likely to appeal to your appetite for wonder and emotion.

catalogue.title: Thunder Road
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling police officer tries to cope with grief while his life unravels.
catalogue.why: Raw character embarrassment and unexpected tenderness; strong Shrinking-meets-dark-comedy potential.

catalogue.title: The Climb
catalogue.synopsis: A pair of lifelong friends repeatedly sabotage one another across years of emotional chaos.
catalogue.why: A sharp, prickly relationship comedy built around flawed people and difficult affection.

catalogue.title: Paddleton
catalogue.synopsis: Two isolated neighbours face a devastating medical decision together.
catalogue.why: Unusually humane male friendship and understated comic warmth; emotionally heavy.

catalogue.title: The Skeleton Twins
catalogue.synopsis: Estranged siblings reunite after personal crises and confront old family wounds.
catalogue.why: Sharp, funny and emotionally raw relationship writing could suit your Shrinking preferences.

catalogue.title: The Kings of Summer
catalogue.synopsis: Three teenagers flee suburban life and build a home in the woods.
catalogue.why: Friendship, freedom and absurd teenage behaviour with an Into the Wild-lite spirit.

catalogue.title: The Eight Mountains
catalogue.synopsis: Two men develop a lifelong friendship through the Italian Alps.
catalogue.why: A breathtaking, patient exploration of friendship, wilderness and the passage of time.

catalogue.title: Tracks
catalogue.synopsis: A young woman crosses the Australian desert with camels and a dog.
catalogue.why: Genuine wilderness and self-discovery make this an obvious extension of Into the Wild.

catalogue.title: Wild
catalogue.synopsis: A woman tackles the Pacific Crest Trail while confronting grief and destructive choices.
catalogue.why: Physical adventure as emotional reckoning, with strong parallels to your favourite travel films.

catalogue.title: The Way Back
catalogue.synopsis: Prisoners escape a Soviet labour camp and embark on an epic journey across Asia.
catalogue.why: A much harsher survival adventure that could appeal to your interest in resilience and travel.

catalogue.title: The Secret of Roan Inish
catalogue.synopsis: A young girl investigates an Irish family's legend about a lost child and selkies.
catalogue.why: Gentle folkloric wonder and a quietly affecting sense of place.

catalogue.title: The Red Turtle
catalogue.synopsis: A castaway builds a mysterious life on an island with a strange giant turtle.
catalogue.why: Almost wordless, visually beautiful storytelling about connection and existence.

catalogue.title: My Life as a Zucchini
catalogue.synopsis: An orphaned boy discovers friendship and belonging in a foster home.
catalogue.why: Brief, funny and deeply moving; a distinctive emotional wildcard.

catalogue.title: Mary and Max
catalogue.synopsis: An unlikely pen-pal friendship grows between an Australian girl and a lonely New Yorker.
catalogue.why: Dark humour and extraordinary tenderness coexist in this adult stop-motion film.

catalogue.title: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
catalogue.synopsis: A tiny living shell becomes a documentary star while searching for family.
catalogue.why: Playful inventiveness and genuine emotional stakes make it strong EEAAO-adjacent comfort viewing.

catalogue.title: Robot Dreams
catalogue.synopsis: A lonely dog builds a robot friend in 1980s New York, but their bond is tested.
catalogue.why: A beautifully simple, wordless friendship story with powerful emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: The Illusionist
catalogue.synopsis: An ageing stage magician befriends a young woman while touring Scotland.
catalogue.why: Quiet, wistful visual storytelling for a reflective evening rather than laughs.

catalogue.title: A Town Called Panic
catalogue.synopsis: Plastic toy characters create utter chaos while attempting to build a birthday present.
catalogue.why: Manic absurdism and commitment to the bit, potentially perfect for your ITYSL side.

catalogue.title: The Triplets of Belleville
catalogue.synopsis: An elderly woman and her dog search for a kidnapped cyclist in a strange city.
catalogue.why: Inventive almost-wordless comedy with a bizarre, singular visual personality.

catalogue.title: Fantastic Planet
catalogue.synopsis: Tiny humans survive oppression on a surreal world dominated by enormous blue aliens.
catalogue.why: Influential and strikingly strange speculative animation, strong worldbuilding wildcard.

catalogue.title: Waking Life
catalogue.synopsis: A man drifts through lucid dreams and philosophical conversations with strangers.
catalogue.why: Formally adventurous and thought-provoking, but potentially too talky for your Donnie Darko reservations.

catalogue.title: A Scanner Darkly
catalogue.synopsis: An undercover narcotics officer loses his identity amid an addictive surveillance culture.
catalogue.why: Distinctive rotoscoping and identity paranoia with a proper plot beneath the ideas.

catalogue.title: The Congress
catalogue.synopsis: An actress sells her digital likeness and enters an animated future shaped by manufactured fantasies.
catalogue.why: Wild philosophical ambition with striking imagery, but intentionally sprawling.

catalogue.title: Beyond the Infinite Two Minutes
catalogue.synopsis: A café owner discovers his computer monitor displays events two minutes into the future.
catalogue.why: A tiny, ingenious time-loop puzzle with charming low-budget comic execution.

catalogue.title: River
catalogue.synopsis: Guests at a Kyoto inn become trapped in a repeating two-minute period.
catalogue.why: An inventive low-budget time puzzle that adds warmth and escalating comedic ingenuity.

catalogue.title: The Infinite Man
catalogue.synopsis: A controlling romantic tries to perfect an anniversary by travelling through time.
catalogue.why: An Australian shoestring brainteaser blending romance, awkwardness and sci-fi mechanisms.

catalogue.title: Timecrimes
catalogue.synopsis: A man spots a mysterious figure and stumbles into an increasingly tangled time loop.
catalogue.why: Compact, sharp temporal plotting offers the type of satisfying mystery you value.

catalogue.title: The Endless
catalogue.synopsis: Brothers revisit the cult they escaped and encounter inexplicable phenomena.
catalogue.why: A patient but rewarding cosmic mystery with atmosphere and properly intriguing revelations.

catalogue.title: Resolution
catalogue.synopsis: A man restrains his addicted friend in a remote cabin as strange recordings appear.
catalogue.why: A small-scale unsettling puzzle; a possible fit if you enjoy mysteries that linger.

catalogue.title: Something in the Dirt
catalogue.synopsis: Two neighbours document strange phenomena in their apartment and chase grand conspiracies.
catalogue.why: A very talky DIY mystery with genuine conceptual ambition; not the safest recommendation.

catalogue.title: Primer
catalogue.synopsis: Two engineers accidentally discover time travel and become caught in its consequences.
catalogue.why: Possibly the densest time-travel puzzle film; made for your full-attention evenings.

catalogue.title: Upstream Color
catalogue.synopsis: Two strangers discover their lives are entangled through a mysterious biological process.
catalogue.why: Very abstract, sensory storytelling with emotional resonance; intentionally elusive.

catalogue.title: The Vast of Night
catalogue.synopsis: A switchboard operator and radio DJ investigate a strange signal in 1950s New Mexico.
catalogue.why: Patient atmospheric storytelling followed by an unusually absorbing science-fiction mystery.

catalogue.title: Prospect
catalogue.synopsis: A teenager and her father search for valuable resources on a poisonous alien moon.
catalogue.why: Exceptional lived-in worldbuilding with tense survival stakes and character dynamics.

catalogue.title: Aniara
catalogue.synopsis: A spaceship carrying emigrants to Mars is knocked irretrievably off course.
catalogue.why: Bleak existential science fiction with a striking premise and major emotional consequences.

catalogue.title: High Life
catalogue.synopsis: Prisoners conduct a dangerous space experiment far from Earth.
catalogue.why: Profoundly strange and disturbing space drama, a riskier arthouse selection.

catalogue.title: Europa Report
catalogue.synopsis: A scientific mission to Jupiter's moon Europa encounters terrifying uncertainty.
catalogue.why: Space exploration and procedural mystery, ideal for your serious sci-fi curiosity.

catalogue.title: I Origins
catalogue.synopsis: A molecular biologist studying eyes encounters discoveries that challenge his worldview.
catalogue.why: An unusual science-and-romance premise aimed at your thoughtful, emotional sci-fi side.

catalogue.title: Another Earth
catalogue.synopsis: The appearance of a duplicate Earth collides with a young woman's guilt and search for redemption.
catalogue.why: A big concept used for a grounded moral and emotional story, potentially strong for you.

catalogue.title: The Man from Earth
catalogue.synopsis: A retiring professor tells colleagues he may have lived for thousands of years.
catalogue.why: A one-room concept film built entirely on conversation; intriguing but requires tolerance for talk.

catalogue.title: The One I Love
catalogue.synopsis: A troubled couple retreat to a holiday house that seems to contain impossible surprises.
catalogue.why: A witty, unnerving relationship puzzle with a high-concept hook and emotional bite.

catalogue.title: The Discovery
catalogue.synopsis: Scientists seemingly prove an afterlife exists, triggering turmoil across society.
catalogue.why: A provocative idea with emotional stakes, but its execution is more uneven.

catalogue.title: The Fare
catalogue.synopsis: A taxi driver picks up a mysterious passenger on an endless road.
catalogue.why: Compact romantic mystery with a clever structural payoff.

catalogue.title: Safety Not Guaranteed
catalogue.synopsis: Journalists investigate a classified ad seeking a companion for time travel.
catalogue.why: Quirky characters and an earnest emotional core inside a very odd premise.

catalogue.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
catalogue.synopsis: Three pub friends become entangled in a series of time-travel paradoxes.
catalogue.why: An accessible British sci-fi comedy whose plotting is smarter than the knockabout presentation.

catalogue.title: The Map of Tiny Perfect Things
catalogue.synopsis: Two teenagers trapped in a time loop discover meaningful details of an ordinary day.
catalogue.why: A lighter cousin to your Eternal Sunshine/Palms Springs interests.

catalogue.title: The Time Traveler's Wife
catalogue.synopsis: A couple struggle with an involuntary genetic condition that sends one partner through time.
catalogue.why: Romantic sci-fi with a bittersweet hook, though more melodrama than mystery.

catalogue.title: Frequency
catalogue.synopsis: A detective communicates with his deceased father through an old radio across time.
catalogue.why: A compelling emotional sci-fi mystery with strong family stakes.

catalogue.title: Deja Vu
catalogue.synopsis: An investigator uses experimental surveillance technology to prevent a devastating bombing.
catalogue.why: Propulsive mystery mechanics without sacrificing an entertaining blockbuster experience.

catalogue.title: The Adjustment Bureau
catalogue.synopsis: A politician learns mysterious agents are controlling the course of his love life.
catalogue.why: Accessible high-concept romance that mixes cosmic intrigue and emotional stakes.

catalogue.title: Good Bye Lenin!
catalogue.synopsis: A son recreates communist East Germany to protect his recovering mother from shocking political change.
catalogue.why: Ingenious comic deception in service of something genuinely loving and moving.

catalogue.title: The Edukators
catalogue.synopsis: Young anti-capitalist activists break into wealthy homes and become involved in a kidnapping.
catalogue.why: Moral argument and youthful idealism with an escalating plot; a political wildcard.

catalogue.title: The Wave
catalogue.synopsis: A teacher's experiment in authoritarianism spirals into a dangerous school movement.
catalogue.why: An engaging premise about institutions and human behaviour that turns genuinely unsettling.

catalogue.title: Force Majeure
catalogue.synopsis: A father's split-second response to an avalanche fractures his family's image of him.
catalogue.why: A brutally funny study of cowardice, ego and relationships; excellent black-comedy candidate.

catalogue.title: The Square
catalogue.synopsis: A museum curator's prestigious exhibition triggers increasingly uncomfortable public scandals.
catalogue.why: Social cringe and vicious satire of cultural institutions, though intentionally sprawling.

catalogue.title: Riders of Justice
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving soldier joins eccentric statisticians in seeking revenge for his wife's death.
catalogue.why: Black humour, complicated men and a proper plot with emotional substance.

catalogue.title: Men & Chicken
catalogue.synopsis: Estranged brothers search for their biological father and uncover grotesque family secrets.
catalogue.why: Extremely odd Scandinavian black comedy for your appetite for committed absurdity.

catalogue.title: The Green Butchers
catalogue.synopsis: Two socially awkward butchers open a shop with a horrible secret ingredient.
catalogue.why: Morbid Danish satire that may appeal to your especially black-comedy moods.

catalogue.title: Adam's Apples
catalogue.synopsis: A neo-Nazi on community service becomes determined to challenge an impossibly optimistic priest.
catalogue.why: Dark theological absurdity and surprisingly touching character work, unlike a conventional feel-good film.

catalogue.title: Speak No Evil
catalogue.synopsis: A Danish family visits charming holiday acquaintances and becomes trapped in mounting discomfort.
catalogue.why: A very bleak escalation of social awkwardness into dread; likely too grim for casual viewing.

catalogue.title: Let the Right One In
catalogue.synopsis: A bullied Swedish boy forms a bond with a mysterious girl living next door.
catalogue.why: Atmospheric horror with a powerful emotional centre, making it a strong Hill House cousin.

catalogue.title: Border
catalogue.synopsis: An unusually perceptive customs officer discovers a startling truth about her origins.
catalogue.why: A bold and uncomfortable fairy tale about identity, desire and belonging.

catalogue.title: Rare Exports
catalogue.synopsis: A Finnish town discovers an ancient and terrifying version of Father Christmas.
catalogue.why: A wonderfully strange holiday horror-comedy with a distinctive sense of mischief.

catalogue.title: Sisu
catalogue.synopsis: A lone gold prospector turns into an unstoppable enemy of retreating Nazis.
catalogue.why: Brutal, gloriously excessive action for evenings when pure spectacle is enough.

catalogue.title: The Man Without a Past
catalogue.synopsis: An amnesiac man rebuilds a humble life among Helsinki's outcasts.
catalogue.why: Deadpan Finnish humour with unexpected humanity and quiet optimism.

catalogue.title: Fallen Leaves
catalogue.synopsis: Two lonely Helsinki workers repeatedly miss chances at finding one another.
catalogue.why: A minimal, gently funny and emotionally rewarding romance with a singular tone.

catalogue.title: The Bothersome Man
catalogue.synopsis: A man wakes in a strangely pleasant city where nothing truly satisfies him.
catalogue.why: Clever, unnerving existential satire for a high-concept mood.

catalogue.title: The Brand New Testament
catalogue.synopsis: God's rebellious daughter escapes their Brussels flat and reveals everyone's date of death.
catalogue.why: A wild theological concept delivered with absurd humour and unexpected tenderness.

catalogue.title: The Extraordinary Journey of the Fakir
catalogue.synopsis: A young Indian magician becomes accidentally entangled in an international odyssey.
catalogue.why: An offbeat, colourful wandering adventure for your Walter Mitty side.

catalogue.title: Micmacs
catalogue.synopsis: A man recruits a group of eccentric misfits to take revenge on arms manufacturers.
catalogue.why: Jeunet's inventive contraptions, ensemble humour and anti-institutional mischief.

catalogue.title: Delicatessen
catalogue.synopsis: Residents of a post-apocalyptic apartment building rely on a butcher with a sinister trade.
catalogue.why: Darkly funny, highly imaginative French cinema with a bizarre self-contained world.

catalogue.title: The City of Lost Children
catalogue.synopsis: A desperate strongman searches a dreamlike harbour city for a stolen child.
catalogue.why: Extravagantly inventive production and dream logic; a captivating visual wildcard.

catalogue.title: A Very Long Engagement
catalogue.synopsis: A young woman searches for the truth behind her fiancé's apparent death in World War I.
catalogue.why: A lovingly constructed historical mystery and romance with huge emotional stakes.

catalogue.title: Mood Indigo
catalogue.synopsis: A whimsical Parisian romance becomes increasingly distorted by an unusual illness.
catalogue.why: Michel Gondry's spectacular craft and emotional surrealism, though the whimsy may divide you.

catalogue.title: The Double
catalogue.synopsis: A timid office worker finds his existence threatened by a charismatic lookalike.
catalogue.why: Bleak, funny workplace paranoia with a surreal premise and a sharp atmosphere.

catalogue.title: Submarine
catalogue.synopsis: An eccentric Welsh teenager tries to save his parents' marriage while pursuing first love.
catalogue.why: Biting adolescent wit mixed with sincere feeling and offbeat British style.

catalogue.title: The Souvenir
catalogue.synopsis: A young film student becomes involved in an increasingly troubling relationship.
catalogue.why: An intimate and demanding portrait of love and self-deception for reflective moods.

catalogue.title: The Souvenir Part II
catalogue.synopsis: A film student processes a damaging relationship by making art from the experience.
catalogue.why: Unusual meta-storytelling about grief and creation, best after its predecessor.

catalogue.title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
catalogue.synopsis: A surgeon's family is drawn into an ominous bargain with a peculiar teenager.
catalogue.why: Unsettling and precise moral horror, but more emotionally cold than Hill House.

catalogue.title: Dogtooth
catalogue.synopsis: Parents raise their adult children in complete isolation under bizarre invented rules.
catalogue.why: Disturbing social control and absurdity; a high-risk Lanthimos experiment.

catalogue.title: Alps
catalogue.synopsis: A group offers to impersonate dead loved ones for grieving families.
catalogue.why: Another unsettling original concept that could fascinate or alienate you.

catalogue.title: The Death of Mr. Lazarescu
catalogue.synopsis: An elderly man is shuffled between Bucharest hospitals as his condition deteriorates.
catalogue.why: Bureaucratic absurdity turned into devastating realism; a challenging institutional satire.

catalogue.title: Toni Erdmann
catalogue.synopsis: A prank-loving father adopts an elaborate persona to reconnect with his corporate daughter.
catalogue.why: Cringe humour collides with sharp corporate satire and a remarkable emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: The Farewell
catalogue.synopsis: A family returns to China under the pretence of a wedding to visit an ill grandmother.
catalogue.why: Excellent family comedy and emotional honesty; a strong Intouchables/Jojo Rabbit recommendation.

catalogue.title: The Namesake
catalogue.synopsis: A son of Bengali immigrants navigates competing cultural expectations across generations.
catalogue.why: A tender multi-generational story about belonging and identity.

catalogue.title: Minari
catalogue.synopsis: A Korean-American family attempts to start a farm in rural Arkansas.
catalogue.why: Warm, funny, emotionally affecting family drama without forced sentimentality.

catalogue.title: The Florida Project
catalogue.synopsis: Children find summer adventures at a motel near Disney World while adults struggle to survive.
catalogue.why: Vivid personalities and childhood wonder sit beside serious emotional stakes.

catalogue.title: American Honey
catalogue.synopsis: A teenager joins a travelling magazine-sales crew across the American Midwest.
catalogue.why: Unruly youthful freedom and travel could echo Into the Wild, with a rougher edge.

catalogue.title: Leave No Trace
catalogue.synopsis: A father and daughter living off-grid in Oregon struggle with reintegration into society.
catalogue.why: Quiet wilderness storytelling and extraordinary emotional restraint.

catalogue.title: The Rider
catalogue.synopsis: A young rodeo rider tries to rebuild his identity after a devastating accident.
catalogue.why: Authentic, moving storytelling about purpose and freedom in wide-open landscapes.

catalogue.title: Sing Street
catalogue.synopsis: A Dublin teenager forms a band to impress a girl and escape family troubles.
catalogue.why: Funny youthful creativity and a generous emotional payoff with great music.

catalogue.title: Once
catalogue.synopsis: A busker and an immigrant bond while writing and recording songs in Dublin.
catalogue.why: Raw, unpretentious romance and creative chemistry; a strong heartfelt-film pick.

catalogue.title: Begin Again
catalogue.synopsis: A songwriter and a struggling music producer make an album across New York.
catalogue.why: Warm, funny creative partnership that might suit your love of uplifting character stories.

catalogue.title: Hearts Beat Loud
catalogue.synopsis: A father and daughter unexpectedly connect through a song they write together.
catalogue.why: An appealing, low-stakes combination of humour, family feeling and music.

catalogue.title: Pride
catalogue.synopsis: London gay activists raise money for striking Welsh miners in the 1980s.
catalogue.why: The sort of funny, uplifting solidarity story that links Jojo Rabbit and Intouchables.

catalogue.title: Brassed Off
catalogue.synopsis: A Yorkshire colliery brass band struggles to survive amid looming pit closures.
catalogue.why: Working-class humour, institutional politics and genuine emotion with local resonance.

catalogue.title: The Full Monty
catalogue.synopsis: Unemployed Sheffield steelworkers stage a strip show to earn money.
catalogue.why: Broad British laughs, strong characters and earned uplift in one classic.

catalogue.title: Billy Elliot
catalogue.synopsis: A miner's son discovers a passion for ballet during a bitter industrial dispute.
catalogue.why: Strong emotional stakes, working-class wit and a triumphant coming-of-age payoff.

catalogue.title: The Angels' Share
catalogue.synopsis: A young offender in Glasgow discovers a talent for whisky tasting and spots a risky opportunity.
catalogue.why: A grounded, funny redemption caper with whisky and big-hearted characters.

catalogue.title: The Old Oak
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling northern pub becomes a flashpoint when Syrian refugees arrive in a former mining community.
catalogue.why: A socially engaged, empathetic British drama that may land with your sentimental side.

catalogue.title: Scrapper
catalogue.synopsis: A resourceful young girl living alone must confront the return of her absent father.
catalogue.why: Funny, imaginative, working-class tenderness with real emotional bite.

catalogue.title: Rye Lane
catalogue.synopsis: Two newly heartbroken Londoners spend a lively day exploring Peckham together.
catalogue.why: Inventive modern romance, comic chemistry and a distinctively colourful style.

catalogue.title: The Kitchen
catalogue.synopsis: A father and son navigate life in London's last surviving social housing estate in a near future.
catalogue.why: Socially grounded speculative fiction with compelling institutional stakes.

catalogue.title: The Last Black Man in San Francisco
catalogue.synopsis: A man tries to reclaim his grandfather's former home in a changing city.
catalogue.why: Highly distinctive urban nostalgia and big feelings, though meditative in pace.

catalogue.title: Blindspotting
catalogue.synopsis: An Oakland parolee tries to survive his final days of probation amid a friendship in crisis.
catalogue.why: Fast, funny and politically sharp storytelling with serious stakes.

catalogue.title: Sorry to Bother You
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling telemarketer finds success by adopting an unusual sales voice, with startling consequences.
catalogue.why: Corporate satire going spectacularly off the rails; a particularly strong wildcard for your taste.

catalogue.title: American Fiction
catalogue.synopsis: A frustrated novelist writes a satirical book that becomes an unlikely cultural sensation.
catalogue.why: Smart media satire balanced with thoughtful family writing and genuine laughs.

catalogue.title: The Book of Clarence
catalogue.synopsis: A hustler in biblical Jerusalem tries to profit from claiming religious significance.
catalogue.why: An irreverent, ambitious mix of satire, spectacle and heartfelt character arcs.

catalogue.title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
catalogue.synopsis: A disgraced megachurch pastor and his wife try to relaunch their public image.
catalogue.why: Institutional hypocrisy and painfully funny self-presentation with documentary-style comedy.

catalogue.title: Jiro Dreams of Sushi
catalogue.synopsis: An elderly Tokyo sushi chef pursues perfection while mentoring his successors.
catalogue.why: An absorbing personality-led craft documentary without true-crime baggage.

catalogue.title: Free Solo
catalogue.synopsis: Climber Alex Honnold prepares to ascend El Capitan without ropes.
catalogue.why: Real-world awe, determination and absurd risk could suit your adventure appetite.

catalogue.title: The Dawn Wall
catalogue.synopsis: Climber Tommy Caldwell attempts an extraordinarily difficult route on El Capitan.
catalogue.why: A moving real adventure built around obsession, resilience and human connection.

catalogue.title: The Alpinist
catalogue.synopsis: A young Canadian climber attempts extraordinary solo ascents while evading attention.
catalogue.why: Hair-raising wilderness footage and enigmatic real-world personality, no crime focus.

catalogue.title: Touching the Void
