catalogue.synopsis: Two climbers recount a disastrous descent in the Peruvian Andes.
catalogue.why: An astonishing survival story with the atmosphere and stakes of a thriller.

catalogue.title: The Rescue
catalogue.synopsis: Divers attempt the dangerous extraction of a youth football team from a flooded Thai cave.
catalogue.why: A spectacular true-life procedural with immense emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: The Biggest Little Farm
catalogue.synopsis: A couple attempts to restore a struggling California farm into a balanced ecosystem.
catalogue.why: Heartfelt real-world ambition and a satisfying long-term transformation.

catalogue.title: My Octopus Teacher
catalogue.synopsis: A filmmaker develops an unusual connection with an octopus in a South African kelp forest.
catalogue.why: Unexpectedly tender natural-history filmmaking with your love of wonder and feeling.

catalogue.title: Fire of Love
catalogue.synopsis: The lives and archive footage of married volcanologists reveal their shared obsession.
catalogue.why: A beautiful, eccentric real-life love story told through an extraordinary adventure.

catalogue.title: The Barkley Marathons
catalogue.synopsis: Runners attempt a near-impossible secretive endurance race in the Tennessee mountains.
catalogue.why: Eccentric characters, physical absurdity and real sporting stakes.

catalogue.title: King of Kong: A Fistful of Quarters
catalogue.synopsis: Two arcade players compete for the Donkey Kong world record amid gaming politics.
catalogue.why: Magnificently petty competition and huge personalities; real-life absurdity without true crime.

catalogue.title: Spellbound
catalogue.synopsis: Eight teenagers prepare for the US national spelling bee.
catalogue.why: A genuinely engaging human competition with unexpectedly memorable personalities.

catalogue.title: American Movie
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling Wisconsin filmmaker attempts to complete his dream horror film.
catalogue.why: An incredibly funny and moving portrait of impossible ambition and eccentric characters.

catalogue.title: The Work
catalogue.synopsis: Outside volunteers join a group-therapy retreat with incarcerated men in California.
catalogue.why: Raw emotional intensity and extraordinary human vulnerability; demanding viewing.

catalogue.title: Searching for Sugar Man
catalogue.synopsis: Fans investigate the mysterious career of a forgotten American musician beloved in South Africa.
catalogue.why: A genuine story of discovery, wonder and profoundly satisfying emotional surprise.

catalogue.title: 20 Feet from Stardom
catalogue.synopsis: Backup singers recount the fame, frustration and artistry behind world-famous music.
catalogue.why: Fantastic personalities and moving stories about creativity and recognition.

catalogue.title: Stop Making Sense
catalogue.synopsis: Talking Heads deliver an inventive and exhilarating staged concert.
catalogue.why: An essential example of how live-performance cinema can be pure joyful invention.

catalogue.title: Koyaanisqatsi
catalogue.synopsis: Wordless images and music contrast natural environments with the pace of industrial life.
catalogue.why: An important experimental work to broaden your cinema vocabulary, not a conventional narrative recommendation.

catalogue.title: Baraka
catalogue.synopsis: A wordless visual journey surveys landscapes, rituals and human life around the world.
catalogue.why: Pure cinematic wonder for reflective moods and your appetite for travel.

catalogue.title: Samsara
catalogue.synopsis: A visually elaborate non-verbal portrait of the world's places and people.
catalogue.why: A visually immersive wildcard rather than a story-led pick.

catalogue.title: The Act of Killing
catalogue.synopsis: Perpetrators of mass killings restage their experiences using movie genres.
catalogue.why: Historically important but deeply disturbing; not a true-crime evening recommendation.

catalogue.title: Ikiru
catalogue.synopsis: A terminally ill civil servant searches for meaning beyond his bureaucratic routine.
catalogue.why: A classic emotional reckoning with institutions and life itself, strongly aligned with your heartfelt side.

catalogue.title: Seven Samurai
catalogue.synopsis: Farmers recruit seven wandering warriors to defend their village from bandits.
catalogue.why: A hugely influential ensemble adventure combining character stakes and compelling action.

catalogue.title: High and Low
catalogue.synopsis: A businessman faces an agonising choice when a kidnapper targets his household.
catalogue.why: One of cinema's great moral thrillers, with escalating plot and social insight.

catalogue.title: Rashomon
catalogue.synopsis: Different witnesses give incompatible accounts of a murder and assault in a forest.
catalogue.why: A foundational storytelling experiment with an engaging central puzzle.

catalogue.title: Yojimbo
catalogue.synopsis: A wandering samurai manipulates rival gangs in a divided town.
catalogue.why: Very entertaining, darkly funny action storytelling that shaped countless later films.

catalogue.title: Harakiri
catalogue.synopsis: A ronin requests ritual suicide and slowly exposes the hypocrisies of a powerful clan.
catalogue.why: Savage institutional critique and devastating reveals: perhaps your ideal historical classic.

catalogue.title: Tokyo Story
catalogue.synopsis: Elderly parents visit their grown children and confront modern family distance.
catalogue.why: An enormously influential study of family feeling, but extremely quiet by your usual standards.

catalogue.title: Late Spring
catalogue.synopsis: A devoted daughter faces the possibility of leaving her widowed father to marry.
catalogue.why: A masterclass in subtle emotional storytelling, an adventurous essential.

catalogue.title: In the Mood for Love
catalogue.synopsis: Two neighbours suspect their spouses of an affair and grow close in restrained secrecy.
catalogue.why: Stunning atmosphere and ache, worth exploring even if you're usually more plot-driven.

catalogue.title: Chungking Express
catalogue.synopsis: Two lonely Hong Kong policemen encounter fleeting connections and unexpected love.
catalogue.why: Playful romantic invention and a singular voice could land very well.

catalogue.title: Fallen Angels
catalogue.synopsis: A contract killer and nocturnal drifters search for connection in neon Hong Kong.
catalogue.why: Visually audacious, restless and emotionally strange; strong style-first wildcard.

catalogue.title: Infernal Affairs
catalogue.synopsis: A police mole within the triads and a gang spy within the police hunt one another.
catalogue.why: Extremely tight cat-and-mouse plotting with complicated divided loyalties.

catalogue.title: The Chaser
catalogue.synopsis: A disgraced detective searches for missing women after discovering a terrifying pattern.
catalogue.why: Fictional crime thriller with brutal tension, but may be too close to true-crime sensibilities.

catalogue.title: The Yellow Sea
catalogue.synopsis: A debt-ridden driver crosses borders for an assassination job that goes wrong.
catalogue.why: Desperate, violent storytelling with twisty stakes and relentless momentum.

catalogue.title: A Bittersweet Life
catalogue.synopsis: A loyal mob enforcer makes one compassionate choice and faces his boss's wrath.
catalogue.why: Stylish revenge tragedy about character, loyalty and escalating consequences.

catalogue.title: The Good, the Bad, the Weird
catalogue.synopsis: Three eccentric gunmen pursue treasure across 1930s Manchuria.
catalogue.why: Stylish madcap action with genuinely entertaining personalities and absurd energy.

catalogue.title: The Host
catalogue.synopsis: A dysfunctional family chases a giant creature after it kidnaps a young girl.
catalogue.why: Bong Joon-ho mixes social satire, monster thrills and real family emotion.

catalogue.title: Mother
catalogue.synopsis: A fiercely protective mother investigates the charge against her troubled son.
catalogue.why: An intricate, unsettling mystery from the director of Parasite with moral complexity.

catalogue.title: Barking Dogs Never Bite
catalogue.synopsis: A frustrated lecturer becomes obsessed with noisy dogs at his apartment complex.
catalogue.why: An early Bong Joon-ho black comedy full of oddball social observation.

catalogue.title: Okja
catalogue.synopsis: A girl tries to rescue her genetically engineered animal companion from a multinational corporation.
catalogue.why: Corporate satire, imaginative spectacle and a genuinely emotional friendship.

catalogue.title: Snowpiercer
catalogue.synopsis: A rebellion erupts aboard a train carrying the remnants of humanity around a frozen planet.
catalogue.why: Sharp class allegory and inventive action from the Parasite filmmaker.

catalogue.title: Joint Security Area
catalogue.synopsis: An incident along the Korean DMZ reveals unexpected ties between soldiers.
catalogue.why: A compelling mystery grounded in character and human connection.

catalogue.title: Burning
catalogue.synopsis: A directionless young man becomes fixated on a charismatic stranger and a vanished woman.
catalogue.why: Slow-burn psychological intrigue with rich ambiguity; suited to your full-attention moods.

catalogue.title: Peppermint Candy
catalogue.synopsis: A man's life unfolds backward through pivotal events against Korean history.
catalogue.why: Ambitious reverse storytelling with devastating emotional consequences.

catalogue.title: A Taxi Driver
catalogue.synopsis: A Seoul taxi driver unexpectedly becomes involved in a dangerous democratic uprising.
catalogue.why: An accessible, engrossing historical drama with a deeply human heart.

catalogue.title: Extreme Job
catalogue.synopsis: A squad of detectives open a fried-chicken restaurant as cover and find accidental success.
catalogue.why: Absolutely ridiculous professional incompetence, surprisingly close to your broad comedy favourites.

catalogue.title: Midnight Runners
catalogue.synopsis: Two trainee police officers launch their own investigation after witnessing an abduction.
catalogue.why: Buddy-comedy energy alongside a brisk detective plot.

catalogue.title: The Man Standing Next
catalogue.synopsis: Senior Korean intelligence figures become embroiled in a political assassination crisis.
catalogue.why: Cold, morally complicated political intrigue for your Succession/Chernobyl tastes.

catalogue.title: Castaway on the Moon
catalogue.synopsis: A stranded office worker begins life on a tiny Seoul river island and draws a reclusive woman's attention.
catalogue.why: Wonderful, funny outsider romance with real emotional and imaginative payoff.

catalogue.title: The Quiet Family
catalogue.synopsis: A family running a remote inn attempts to conceal an unfortunate series of guest deaths.
catalogue.why: Korean black farce where increasingly terrible decisions multiply.

catalogue.title: Save the Green Planet!
catalogue.synopsis: A conspiracy theorist kidnaps a businessman he believes is an extraterrestrial.
catalogue.why: Wild tonal shifts, outrageous humour and paranoid science fiction for adventurous evenings.

catalogue.title: Welcome to Dongmakgol
catalogue.synopsis: Enemy soldiers become stranded together in a peaceful Korean mountain village.
catalogue.why: A strange blend of wartime satire, eccentric comedy and sentiment.

catalogue.title: The Taste of Tea
catalogue.synopsis: An eccentric Japanese family encounters quiet crises and surreal everyday visions.
catalogue.why: Gentle, surreal family comedy that broadens the weird-but-warm axis.

catalogue.title: One Million Yen Girl
catalogue.synopsis: A young woman repeatedly moves towns, saving money while looking for herself.
catalogue.why: A modest yet lovely self-discovery journey for your Into the Wild side.

catalogue.title: Shoplifters
catalogue.synopsis: A family surviving on petty theft takes in a neglected young girl.
catalogue.why: Complex, warm and heartbreaking writing about what makes a family.

catalogue.title: Nobody Knows
catalogue.synopsis: Four abandoned children try to keep their Tokyo apartment household together.
catalogue.why: Patient, devastatingly humane storytelling; emotionally demanding but worthwhile.

catalogue.title: Monster
catalogue.synopsis: A mother confronts a school when her son's behaviour changes, revealing conflicting perspectives.
catalogue.why: Layered narrative revelations and huge emotional resonance reward close attention.

catalogue.title: After Life
catalogue.synopsis: The newly dead must choose one memory to preserve for eternity.
catalogue.why: A beautiful and original thought experiment about the value of ordinary lives.

catalogue.title: Drive My Car
catalogue.synopsis: A widowed theatre director and his driver slowly reveal grief through work and conversation.
catalogue.why: A masterfully moving, deliberately slow film for your more contemplative moods.

catalogue.title: Perfect Days
catalogue.synopsis: A Tokyo toilet cleaner finds purpose in small daily rituals and relationships.
catalogue.why: A life-affirming minimalism experiment; interesting contrast with Walter Mitty's bigger ambitions.

catalogue.title: Tampopo
catalogue.synopsis: A truck driver helps a widow turn her ramen shop into the best in town.
catalogue.why: A delicious, funny and unexpectedly inventive tribute to food and companionship.

catalogue.title: Departures
catalogue.synopsis: An unemployed cellist takes a job preparing the dead for funerals.
catalogue.why: A quirky setup becomes profoundly moving and humane, with lovely comic detail.

catalogue.title: Shall We Dance?
catalogue.synopsis: A discontented salaryman secretly takes ballroom dance lessons and rediscovers joy.
catalogue.why: Warm, funny personal transformation that could delight your uplifting-story side.

catalogue.title: Linda Linda Linda
catalogue.synopsis: Schoolgirls race to form a band for their school's music festival.
catalogue.why: Gentle friendship and authentic creative joy, a light international gem.

catalogue.title: Hausu
catalogue.synopsis: Schoolgirls visit an aunt's country house and confront wildly surreal supernatural attacks.
catalogue.why: An outrageous cult horror experience, nearly pure visual insanity.

catalogue.title: Cure
catalogue.synopsis: A detective investigates a series of unrelated murders sharing a disturbing pattern.
catalogue.why: Masterful creeping psychological dread and one of the most haunting mysteries in cinema.

catalogue.title: Pulse
catalogue.synopsis: A mysterious internet phenomenon spreads loneliness and supernatural terror across Tokyo.
catalogue.why: Existential atmosphere and frightening ideas, closely aligned with Hill House's dread.

catalogue.title: Noroi: The Curse
catalogue.synopsis: A paranormal documentarian traces seemingly unrelated incidents to a sinister folk ritual.
catalogue.why: A slow accumulation of clues and supernatural unease; unusually strong horror mystery.

catalogue.title: One Missed Call
catalogue.synopsis: People receive phone messages apparently recording their own future deaths.
catalogue.why: A neat high-concept horror mystery, though more genre-mechanical than emotional.

catalogue.title: Audition
catalogue.synopsis: A widower uses a fake casting call to find romance and discovers horrifying secrets.
catalogue.why: A landmark slow-burn shocker that tests your appetite for unsettling horror.

catalogue.title: The Night House
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving widow investigates disturbing secrets in the lakeside home her husband built.
catalogue.why: Character-driven grief and carefully constructed supernatural intrigue make a good Hill House match.

catalogue.title: The Empty Man
catalogue.synopsis: An ex-police officer investigates a missing girl and a mysterious urban legend.
catalogue.why: Surprisingly ambitious cosmic horror with layers of mystery rather than cheap shocks.

catalogue.title: The Autopsy of Jane Doe
catalogue.synopsis: A father and son examine an unidentified corpse whose body defies explanation.
catalogue.why: A wonderfully efficient and escalating supernatural investigation.

catalogue.title: The Dark and the Wicked
catalogue.synopsis: Siblings returning to their family farm confront a crushing supernatural presence.
catalogue.why: Extremely bleak dread and little comic relief; reserved for dark moods.

catalogue.title: Relic
catalogue.synopsis: Three generations of women confront a grandmother's disappearance and a sinister family home.
catalogue.why: Intimate supernatural horror using family emotion in a Hill House-like way.

catalogue.title: Lake Mungo
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving family investigates strange footage after their daughter's death.
catalogue.why: Subtle documentary-style ghost story with real emotional weight and unnerving reveals.

catalogue.title: The Orphanage
catalogue.synopsis: A woman returns to her childhood orphanage and her young son disappears.
catalogue.why: A deeply emotional gothic mystery with haunting family stakes.

catalogue.title: The Devil's Backbone
catalogue.synopsis: Boys in a remote orphanage during the Spanish Civil War encounter a restless ghost.
catalogue.why: Beautiful period atmosphere and grief-driven supernatural storytelling.

catalogue.title: Pan's Labyrinth
catalogue.synopsis: A young girl retreats into a dangerous mythic world amid Spain's fascist repression.
catalogue.why: A masterpiece of inventive fantasy and devastating emotional truth.

catalogue.title: The Shape of Water
catalogue.synopsis: A mute cleaner falls in love with an amphibious captive in a secret facility.
catalogue.why: Unusual romance, institutional cruelty and emotionally sincere fantasy.

catalogue.title: Crimson Peak
catalogue.synopsis: A young writer moves into an eerie English mansion with her mysterious husband.
catalogue.why: Gothic atmosphere and emotional mystery, with sumptuous visual storytelling.

catalogue.title: A Ghost Story
catalogue.synopsis: A ghost silently watches time pass in the home he once shared with his partner.
catalogue.why: A radical experiment in time, grief and love; rewarding but extremely slow.

catalogue.title: The Awakening
catalogue.synopsis: A sceptical ghost investigator visits a boarding school after reports of a haunting.
catalogue.why: Traditional gothic intrigue and atmosphere, an accessible post-Others possibility.

catalogue.title: The Innocents
catalogue.synopsis: A governess becomes convinced the children under her care are influenced by ghosts.
catalogue.why: A foundational psychological ghost story rich in ambiguity and dread.

catalogue.title: The Changeling
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving composer moves into a mansion where unexplained disturbances begin.
catalogue.why: Classic haunted-house investigation and emotionally grounded supernatural intrigue.

catalogue.title: The Wicker Man
catalogue.synopsis: A Scottish policeman investigates a missing child on an isolated pagan island.
catalogue.why: Folk horror as a carefully unfolding investigation with a magnificent final payoff.

catalogue.title: Don't Look Now
catalogue.synopsis: Grieving parents encounter disturbing visions while living in Venice.
catalogue.why: Haunting imagery and deeply felt grief, an important atmospheric classic.

catalogue.title: The Vanishing
catalogue.synopsis: A man searches obsessively for his girlfriend after she disappears at a service station.
catalogue.why: A masterclass in psychological suspense with a devastating, concrete resolution.

catalogue.title: The Hidden Face
catalogue.synopsis: A musician's girlfriend vanishes as his new relationship reveals hidden secrets.
catalogue.why: A very effective Spanish-language twisty mystery with accessible thrills.

catalogue.title: Sleep Tight
catalogue.synopsis: A Barcelona concierge secretly torments the residents of his building.
catalogue.why: A nasty psychological thriller about malicious obsession; powerful but unpleasant.

catalogue.title: The Invisible Guest
catalogue.synopsis: A businessman accused of murder prepares his defence with a brilliant lawyer.
catalogue.why: Ingenious twists and tightly engineered revelations exactly suit your plot-first side.

catalogue.title: Mirage
catalogue.synopsis: A woman uses an impossible temporal connection to save a boy, changing her family life.
catalogue.why: High-concept time mechanics and a tense emotional mystery.

catalogue.title: The Body
catalogue.synopsis: A corpse disappears from a morgue and a police investigation unearths a web of secrets.
catalogue.why: Compelling, twist-driven Spanish thriller likely to satisfy your love of revelations.

catalogue.title: Marshland
catalogue.synopsis: Two detectives investigate disappearances in the marshes of post-Franco Spain.
catalogue.why: An engrossing fictional mystery with striking atmosphere and institutional tensions.

catalogue.title: Tell No One
catalogue.synopsis: A widower receives evidence suggesting his murdered wife might still be alive.
catalogue.why: Exceptionally propulsive French mystery with strong emotional stakes.

catalogue.title: Headhunters
catalogue.synopsis: A corporate recruiter secretly steals art until he targets the wrong man.
catalogue.why: Vicious, twisty Scandinavian crime caper with escalating absurdity.

catalogue.title: The Guilty
catalogue.synopsis: A Danish emergency dispatcher tries to save a caller using only a telephone.
catalogue.why: A superbly tight one-location thriller with clever reversals.

catalogue.title: The Secret in Their Eyes
catalogue.synopsis: A retired Argentine investigator revisits an unresolved case and a lost love.
catalogue.why: Superb mystery plotting woven with years of regret and emotional consequences.

catalogue.title: Nine Queens
catalogue.synopsis: Two Buenos Aires swindlers attempt a complex deal involving rare forged stamps.
catalogue.why: A delicious con-artist puzzle about trust and betrayal.

catalogue.title: The Distinguished Citizen
catalogue.synopsis: A Nobel laureate returns to the provincial town that inspired his writing and creates scandal.
catalogue.why: Literary ego, social satire and slow-motion comic disaster.

catalogue.title: The Clan
catalogue.synopsis: A seemingly respectable Argentine family is revealed to run a kidnapping operation.
catalogue.why: Disturbing historical crime drama; less ideal given your true-crime dislike.

catalogue.title: The Aura
catalogue.synopsis: An epileptic taxidermist stumbles into an opportunity to execute a perfect crime.
catalogue.why: A moody Argentine cerebral thriller with an unusually introspective lead.

catalogue.title: Amores Perros
catalogue.synopsis: Lives collide through a car accident across three stories in Mexico City.
catalogue.why: Vivid, ambitious interconnected storytelling with strong moral and emotional impact.

catalogue.title: Y tu mamá también
catalogue.synopsis: Two teenagers and an older woman take a life-changing road trip across Mexico.
catalogue.why: Road-trip freedom, messy comedy and bittersweet emotional maturity.

catalogue.title: Roma
catalogue.synopsis: A housekeeper navigates family upheaval in 1970s Mexico City.
catalogue.why: A stunning personal epic, rewarding when you're in the mood for patient observation.

catalogue.title: City of God
catalogue.synopsis: Young people navigate the rise of organised gangs in a Rio favela.
catalogue.why: Energetic, expertly structured storytelling with an indelible world and characters.

catalogue.title: Elite Squad
catalogue.synopsis: A brutal Rio police unit confronts gang violence and corruption.
catalogue.why: Hard-hitting fictionalised institutional drama, potentially compelling but relentlessly violent.

catalogue.title: Central Station
catalogue.synopsis: A retired teacher and a boy journey across Brazil looking for his father.
catalogue.why: A deeply moving road movie and exactly the sort of human connection you often love.

catalogue.title: The Second Mother
catalogue.synopsis: A live-in housekeeper's daughter disrupts the class hierarchy of a wealthy household.
catalogue.why: Warmth, character clashes and astute institutional satire.

catalogue.title: Bacurau
catalogue.synopsis: A remote Brazilian village discovers it has mysteriously vanished from digital maps.
catalogue.why: A wonderfully unpredictable blend of social satire, genre thrills and communal resistance.

catalogue.title: The Invisible Life of Eurídice Gusmão
catalogue.synopsis: Separated sisters in 1950s Rio struggle against family expectations and oppressive choices.
catalogue.why: An intense and beautifully made emotional drama, reserved for heavier evenings.

catalogue.title: The Man Who Copied
catalogue.synopsis: A humble photocopier operator devises an elaborate scheme to win a neighbour's affection.
catalogue.why: A charmingly odd Brazilian comic crime plot with a surprising trajectory.

catalogue.title: The 100-Year-Old Man Who Climbed Out the Window and Disappeared
catalogue.synopsis: A centenarian flees his care home and becomes entangled in crime and outrageous history.
catalogue.why: A goofy, colourful adventure that connects your Forrest Gump and absurdist comedy tastes.

catalogue.title: A Man Called Ove
catalogue.synopsis: A cantankerous widower develops unexpected ties with his new neighbours.
catalogue.why: A moving combination of prickly characters and earned warmth, good Shrinking territory.

catalogue.title: The 101-Year-Old Man Who Skipped Out on the Bill and Disappeared
catalogue.synopsis: An eccentric retired spy sets off across Europe in search of a valuable Soviet soda recipe.
catalogue.why: An absurd globe-trotting sequel for nights when you want ridiculous characters and a daft adventure.

catalogue.title: Oslo, August 31st
catalogue.synopsis: A man recovering from addiction spends a day reconnecting with Oslo and old acquaintances.
catalogue.why: Formally beautiful and deeply sad; a demanding counterpoint to uplifting favourites.

catalogue.title: Reprise
catalogue.synopsis: Two aspiring writers experience friendship, jealousy and mental-health struggles.
catalogue.why: Energetic storytelling, ambition and difficult friendships, with a touch of Kaufman-style self-awareness.

catalogue.title: Thelma
catalogue.synopsis: A sheltered university student discovers strange abilities linked to forbidden desires.
catalogue.why: Elegant psychological mystery with emotional and supernatural dimensions.

catalogue.title: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
catalogue.synopsis: A lonely vampire wanders an Iranian ghost town and becomes entangled in local lives.
catalogue.why: Stylish, moody outsider romance that expands your horror taste beyond scares.

catalogue.title: Under the Shadow
catalogue.synopsis: A mother and daughter experience strange disturbances during wartime Tehran.
catalogue.why: Excellent domestic dread linked to historical and maternal anxiety.

catalogue.title: His House
catalogue.synopsis: A refugee couple settles into a British home haunted by their past.
catalogue.why: A powerful haunted-house film with real emotional and political substance.

catalogue.title: Talk to Me
catalogue.synopsis: Teenagers use an embalmed hand to contact spirits with devastating consequences.
catalogue.why: An inventive supernatural hook, effective mystery and strong emotional consequences.

catalogue.title: Oddity
catalogue.synopsis: A blind psychic investigates her sister's death using uncanny antiques.
catalogue.why: Compact, excellent supernatural mystery with carefully delivered scares.

catalogue.title: Caveat
catalogue.synopsis: A man accepts a strange caretaking job in an isolated house with deeply unsettling rules.
catalogue.why: Slow-burn dread and a genuinely bizarre central mystery.

catalogue.title: The Vigil
catalogue.synopsis: A man keeps watch over a corpse overnight and encounters a malevolent presence.
catalogue.why: Tightly focused folk-religious horror driven by claustrophobia and grief.

catalogue.title: The Ritual
catalogue.synopsis: Four friends hiking through Swedish forests discover ancient threats and old resentments.
catalogue.why: Wilderness unease, fractured friendship and an engaging creature mystery.

catalogue.title: A Dark Song
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving mother rents an isolated house for an elaborate occult ritual.
catalogue.why: Extremely patient, unusual ritual horror built around loss and purpose.

catalogue.title: The Blackcoat's Daughter
catalogue.synopsis: Two girls remain at a boarding school over break as sinister events unfold.
catalogue.why: Deliberate atmosphere and structural mystery, possibly too chilly for casual nights.

catalogue.title: Saint Maud
catalogue.synopsis: A devout nurse becomes dangerously fixated on saving her patient's soul.
catalogue.why: Tense psychological character study with a genuinely unsettling progression.

catalogue.title: The Lodge
catalogue.synopsis: A woman and two children become snowbound in a holiday cabin amid disturbing events.
catalogue.why: Bleak, slow-building paranoia that could appeal to your psychological horror taste.

catalogue.title: Possessor
catalogue.synopsis: An assassin uses mind-control technology to inhabit other people's bodies.
catalogue.why: Ruthless high-concept science fiction with strong visual identity and extreme violence.

catalogue.title: Infinity Pool
catalogue.synopsis: Tourists at a luxurious resort discover horrifying privileges enjoyed by the wealthy.
catalogue.why: Provocative identity horror and satire, but colder and more grotesque than your favourites.

catalogue.title: The Substance
catalogue.synopsis: An ageing celebrity tries a secret drug that creates a younger version of herself.
catalogue.why: Grotesque, savage celebrity satire with an outrageously committed visual premise.

catalogue.title: The Neon Demon
catalogue.synopsis: A young model enters Los Angeles fashion culture and confronts predatory obsession.
catalogue.why: Stylish, disturbing satire with far more atmosphere than narrative warmth.

catalogue.title: Raw
catalogue.synopsis: A veterinary student develops frightening appetites after a hazing ritual.
catalogue.why: Striking body horror grounded in identity, family tension and character transformation.

catalogue.title: Titane
catalogue.synopsis: A violent woman's strange bodily transformation leads her into an unlikely new family.
catalogue.why: One of the wildest body-horror films around, with surprising human tenderness.

catalogue.title: The Skin I Live In
catalogue.synopsis: A brilliant surgeon conducts disturbing experiments amid a web of buried personal secrets.
catalogue.why: A provocative, meticulously plotted psychological mystery from Almodóvar.

catalogue.title: Talk to Her
catalogue.synopsis: Two men form an unlikely friendship while caring for women in comas.
catalogue.why: Complex, ethically uncomfortable emotional storytelling with a distinctive voice.

catalogue.title: Volver
catalogue.synopsis: Women in a Spanish family confront grief, secrets and the apparent return of their mother.
catalogue.why: Warmth, absurdity and complicated family relationships in a colourful mystery.

catalogue.title: All About My Mother
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving woman journeys to reconnect with people from her past.
catalogue.why: Vibrant character writing and huge emotional generosity beneath messy circumstances.

catalogue.title: Parallel Mothers
catalogue.synopsis: Two women who give birth on the same day develop complicated, historically rooted ties.
catalogue.why: Ambitious family melodrama with secrets and moral questions.

catalogue.title: Pain and Glory
catalogue.synopsis: An ageing film director reflects on childhood, love and creative block.
catalogue.why: Thoughtful and deeply felt storytelling about life and artistic memory.

catalogue.title: The Piano Teacher
catalogue.synopsis: A repressed music professor enters a dangerous relationship with a student.
catalogue.why: An intensely uncomfortable character study, more challenging than a conventional thriller.

catalogue.title: Cache
catalogue.synopsis: A Parisian couple receive anonymous surveillance tapes that expose buried guilt.
catalogue.why: A masterful slow-burn psychological mystery, though deliberately refuses tidy answers.

catalogue.title: The White Ribbon
catalogue.synopsis: Strange incidents unsettle a German village before the First World War.
catalogue.why: Elegant, chilling social mystery about repression and institutional violence.

catalogue.title: Funny Games
catalogue.synopsis: A vacationing family is subjected to torment by two intruders.
catalogue.why: A deliberately alienating horror experiment, included for adventurous completism rather than comfort.

catalogue.title: Amour
catalogue.synopsis: An elderly Parisian couple confront the consequences of a debilitating stroke.
catalogue.why: Profound and devastating intimacy; a formidable essential for the right evening.

catalogue.title: The Other Two
catalogue.synopsis: Two struggling adult siblings resent their teenage brother's sudden pop stardom.
catalogue.why: Razor-sharp entertainment-industry satire with excellent jokes and messy characters.

catalogue.title: Search Party
catalogue.synopsis: Self-absorbed Brooklyn friends investigate a missing acquaintance and create escalating disasters.
catalogue.why: The blend of mystery and terrible people could be an especially good Sunny-meets-plot match.

catalogue.title: Corporate
catalogue.synopsis: Two junior employees endure the bleak absurdities of an enormous corporation.
catalogue.why: Vicious workplace satire with far more cynicism than Parks or Superstore.

catalogue.title: Review
catalogue.synopsis: A television host reviews everyday life experiences and gradually destroys his own life.
catalogue.why: A wonderfully committed absurd premise that escalates to genuinely bleak consequences.

catalogue.title: The Increasingly Poor Decisions of Todd Margaret
catalogue.synopsis: An incompetent American businessman blunders into disastrous lies while managing a London sales operation.
catalogue.why: Spectacular comic humiliation in the spirit of Peep Show and The Office.

catalogue.title: Flowers
catalogue.synopsis: A creatively troubled family struggles with mental illness, intimacy and eccentric routines.
catalogue.why: Exceptionally strange British comedy with an enormous emotional heart.

catalogue.title: This Way Up
catalogue.synopsis: An Irish teacher in London rebuilds her life after a mental-health crisis.
catalogue.why: Sharp character humour and moving relationships, very credible for your Shrinking side.

catalogue.title: Such Brave Girls
catalogue.synopsis: A mother and her daughters survive catastrophically dysfunctional romantic and financial lives.
catalogue.why: Deliciously nasty character comedy with frank emotional undertones.

catalogue.title: Am I Being Unreasonable?
catalogue.synopsis: A lonely mother develops an intense friendship that hides increasingly strange secrets.
catalogue.why: British black comedy plus an addictive mystery, a particularly promising combination.

catalogue.title: The Change
catalogue.synopsis: A middle-aged woman leaves her family behind to rediscover herself in a forest community.
catalogue.why: Sharp, warm British oddball comedy with a gentle escape fantasy.

catalogue.title: Dreaming Whilst Black
catalogue.synopsis: An aspiring filmmaker tries to pursue his ambitions amid family, work and cultural pressures.
catalogue.why: Excellent character-driven comedy about creative frustration and messy real lives.

catalogue.title: We Are Lady Parts
catalogue.synopsis: A shy student joins an outspoken all-women Muslim punk band.
catalogue.why: Distinctive comic personalities and music with real warmth and originality.

catalogue.title: Big Boys
catalogue.synopsis: A shy university fresher bonds with a confident roommate while processing grief.
catalogue.why: A very funny and surprisingly moving British friendship comedy.

catalogue.title: Ladhood
catalogue.synopsis: A Yorkshireman revisits the formative mistakes of his teenage years.
catalogue.why: Awkward humour, Northern detail and self-deprecating character writing.

catalogue.title: Alma's Not Normal
catalogue.synopsis: A Bolton woman struggles to build a more fulfilling life amid chaotic family circumstances.
catalogue.why: A highly distinctive, funny and big-hearted Northern comedy.

catalogue.title: People Just Do Nothing
catalogue.synopsis: A hopeless group of pirate-radio DJs pursue delusional dreams of fame in West London.
catalogue.why: The Office-style format but with exceptionally daft personalities and committed jokes.

catalogue.title: Stath Lets Flats
catalogue.synopsis: An incompetent letting agent attempts to prove his worth in his father's business.
catalogue.why: Extraordinary verbal stupidity and cringe might hit your I Think You Should Leave appetite.

catalogue.title: Friday Night Dinner
catalogue.synopsis: Two grown sons visit their parents for weekly dinners that descend into chaos.
catalogue.why: Strong recurring character humour, increasingly absurd family rituals and quotable lines.

catalogue.title: The Inbetweeners
catalogue.synopsis: Four deeply uncool sixth-form boys experience humiliating disasters while trying to grow up.
catalogue.why: A major British outrageous-comedy touchstone for your Superbad and Peep Show taste.

catalogue.title: Fresh Meat
catalogue.synopsis: University housemates form complicated friendships while navigating disasters and identities.
catalogue.why: Awkward ensemble comedy with character development and significant emotional payoff.

catalogue.title: Green Wing
catalogue.synopsis: A hospital becomes the setting for surreal staff rivalries and strange romantic disasters.
catalogue.why: Deeply silly British surrealism; a useful test of your comedy taste.

catalogue.title: Black Books
catalogue.synopsis: A misanthropic bookshop owner and friends turn daily life into rude comic chaos.
catalogue.why: Terrible people, sharp writing and beautifully nasty dialogue.

catalogue.title: Spaced
catalogue.synopsis: Two strangers pretend to be a couple to rent a flat and meet eccentric Londoners.
catalogue.why: Inventive visual comedy and genre references with surprisingly good friendship writing.

catalogue.title: The IT Crowd
catalogue.synopsis: A hopeless basement technology department deals with absurd corporate crises.
catalogue.why: Big idiotic jokes and institutional incompetence, despite a broad sitcom format.

catalogue.title: Garth Marenghi's Darkplace
catalogue.synopsis: A pompous horror author presents his outrageously terrible 1980s television drama.
catalogue.why: Meta absurdity and totally committed comic incompetence, a strong ITYSL candidate.

catalogue.title: Toast of London
catalogue.synopsis: A pompous struggling actor stumbles through auditions and disastrous personal choices.
catalogue.why: Matt Berry's outrageous performance and deliberately bizarre jokes might win you over despite Shadows.

catalogue.title: Snuff Box
catalogue.synopsis: Two eccentric hangmen conduct absurd conversations and surreal musical interludes.
catalogue.why: Unapologetically weird British sketch comedy for your experimental-comedy nights.

catalogue.title: A Touch of Cloth
catalogue.synopsis: A troubled detective investigates murders in a wildly exaggerated police-drama parody.
catalogue.why: Relentless sight gags and stupid wordplay; essentially an extended Naked Gun joke.

catalogue.title: The Day Today
catalogue.synopsis: A fake British news programme reports absurd events with total seriousness.
catalogue.why: A canonical satire from the creators of much of the humour you already love.

catalogue.title: Brass Eye
catalogue.synopsis: A spoof current-affairs series exposes media sensationalism and public gullibility.
catalogue.why: Ferocious, transgressive media satire with unmistakable connections to Four Lions.

catalogue.title: Jam
catalogue.synopsis: Surreal sketches explore deeply unsettling situations and nightmare logic.
catalogue.why: An extreme and uncomfortable Chris Morris experiment, almost the dark edge of your comic taste.

catalogue.title: The Armando Iannucci Shows
catalogue.synopsis: Armando Iannucci explores modern life's irritations through surreal sketches.
catalogue.why: A deeper cut into the absurd institutional comedy behind your love of The Thick of It.

catalogue.title: Time Trumpet
catalogue.synopsis: A fake future documentary looks back on ridiculous invented events from recent history.
catalogue.why: Iannucci's media satire turned into an absurd retrospective.

catalogue.title: Look Around You
catalogue.synopsis: Deadpan parodies of educational science programmes deliver increasingly absurd discoveries.
catalogue.why: Elegant, highly specific absurd jokes that may suit your ITYSL and Nathan tastes.

catalogue.title: The Mighty Boosh
catalogue.synopsis: Two eccentric friends embark on surreal adventures through impossible landscapes.
catalogue.why: An influential cult oddity where sheer comic creativity matters more than plot.

catalogue.title: Flight of the Conchords
catalogue.synopsis: Two New Zealand musicians struggle to become famous in New York.
catalogue.why: Brilliantly dry, silly character humour with inventive musical jokes.

catalogue.title: The Young Ones
catalogue.synopsis: Four wildly incompatible students live together in a crumbling house.
catalogue.why: Foundational anarchic British sitcom energy, with deeply stupid character behaviour.

catalogue.title: Bottom
catalogue.synopsis: Two unemployed flatmates squabble violently through a life of spectacular failure.
catalogue.why: A genuine UK cult sitcom with aggressive physical absurdity and horrible characters.

catalogue.title: Father Ted
catalogue.synopsis: Three disgraced priests and their housekeeper live on a remote Irish island.
catalogue.why: Extraordinary comic character combinations and reliable escalating silliness.

catalogue.title: The League of Gentlemen
catalogue.synopsis: Residents of an extremely strange English town harbour disturbing secrets.
catalogue.why: Black British humour and nightmare absurdity, potential crossover with your Hill House mood.

catalogue.title: Psychoville
catalogue.synopsis: A set of eccentric strangers receive anonymous messages about secrets they share.
catalogue.why: An unusually good mixture of grotesque comedy and an unfolding mystery.

catalogue.title: The Cleaner
catalogue.synopsis: A crime-scene cleaner meets the eccentric people left behind after deaths.
catalogue.why: Personality-led black comedy with one-off characters, despite its crime-adjacent setting.

catalogue.title: Mandy
catalogue.synopsis: A chaotic woman pursues absurd job schemes and personal goals around England.
catalogue.why: Near-cartoonish physical comedy for your truly ridiculous moods.

catalogue.title: The Outlaws
catalogue.synopsis: Community-service offenders stumble into trouble after discovering a criminal's money.
catalogue.why: A comedy ensemble with a continuing crime plot and meaningful relationships.

catalogue.title: Mr Inbetween
catalogue.synopsis: An Australian criminal balances violent work with parenting and ordinary life.
catalogue.why: Exceptionally sharp dark humour, grounded character writing and propulsive short episodes.

catalogue.title: The Tourist
catalogue.synopsis: An amnesiac man wakes in rural Australia with dangerous people pursuing him.
catalogue.why: An engaging puzzle with offbeat humour and an evolving identity mystery.

catalogue.title: Deadloch
catalogue.synopsis: Two deeply mismatched detectives investigate killings in a Tasmanian town.
catalogue.why: A genuinely funny fictional whodunnit driven by abrasive character dynamics.

catalogue.title: Fisk
catalogue.synopsis: A no-nonsense lawyer takes a job at a small suburban wills-and-probate firm.
catalogue.why: Excellent dry character comedy with painfully funny workplace encounters.

catalogue.title: Upright
catalogue.synopsis: Two damaged strangers road-trip across Australia with a prized piano.
catalogue.why: Witty, warm and genuinely affecting adventure, a strong Walter Mitty/Shrinking overlap.

catalogue.title: The Letdown
catalogue.synopsis: A new mother navigates sleep deprivation, relationships and unexpected social pressures.
catalogue.why: Honest adult humour with a strong emotional streak.

catalogue.title: No Activity
catalogue.synopsis: Two detectives endure endless stakeouts amid ridiculous police conversations.
catalogue.why: Deadpan character banter where the joke is everything.

catalogue.title: The Moodys
catalogue.synopsis: An Australian family reunites across holidays and creates reliably awful tension.
catalogue.why: An abrasive family-ensemble comedy for a casual evening.

catalogue.title: Please Like Me
catalogue.synopsis: An awkward young man navigates adulthood, relationships and family mental-health problems.
catalogue.why: Funny, messy and devastatingly honest character storytelling.

catalogue.title: Hacks
catalogue.synopsis: A veteran comedian and a young writer form a prickly partnership in Las Vegas.
catalogue.why: Savage jokes and earned affection through deeply flawed central characters.

catalogue.title: Somebody Somewhere
catalogue.synopsis: A woman reconnects with herself and an unexpected community in small-town Kansas.
catalogue.why: An unusually natural, funny and moving character show for your warmth-seeking moods.

catalogue.title: Better Things
catalogue.synopsis: A working actress raises three daughters while juggling a messy family life.
catalogue.why: Sharp, human observational humour with deep emotional honesty.

catalogue.title: High Maintenance
catalogue.synopsis: A Brooklyn cannabis courier becomes a link between wildly different New Yorkers.
catalogue.why: An inventive anthology of flawed people and unexpected emotional connections.

catalogue.title: Baskets
catalogue.synopsis: An aspiring professional clown returns to Bakersfield and struggles with his family.
catalogue.why: Painful awkwardness and strange tenderness might connect to your love of Frank.

catalogue.title: Kidding
catalogue.synopsis: A beloved children's presenter begins to unravel after a family tragedy.
catalogue.why: Jim Carrey in a high-concept tragicomedy about grief, performance and identity.

catalogue.title: The Afterparty
catalogue.synopsis: Guests at a school reunion recount the same possible murder through different genre perspectives.
catalogue.why: A genuinely clever fictional mystery built around changing storytelling styles and jokes.

catalogue.title: The Resort
catalogue.synopsis: A holidaying couple investigates a disappearance tied to an abandoned resort.
catalogue.why: Playful high-concept puzzle storytelling with oddball characters.

catalogue.title: Murderville
catalogue.synopsis: A detective and an unprepared celebrity guest improvise their way through fictional investigations.
catalogue.why: The commitment to ridiculous bits offers a rare genuinely funny crime-comedy format.

catalogue.title: The Flight Attendant
catalogue.synopsis: A flight attendant wakes beside a dead man and tries to piece together the previous night.
catalogue.why: An addictive, heightened thriller with dark comedy and unreliable memories.

catalogue.title: Made for Love
catalogue.synopsis: A woman flees her controlling technology-mogul husband and his invasive brain implant.
catalogue.why: Dark tech satire and disturbing relationship dynamics, strong Black Mirror crossover.

catalogue.title: Living with Yourself
catalogue.synopsis: A depressed man undergoes an experimental treatment that creates a superior version of himself.
catalogue.why: Identity sci-fi played for comedy with real relationship consequences.

catalogue.title: Upload
catalogue.synopsis: A young programmer enters a luxury digital afterlife after a suspicious death.
catalogue.why: Funny ideas about technology and capitalism wrapped in a serialised mystery.

catalogue.title: Forever
catalogue.synopsis: A married couple's predictable life takes a startling metaphysical turn.
catalogue.why: A deceptively gentle high-concept relationship story with surprising depth.

catalogue.title: The Good Lord Bird
catalogue.synopsis: A teenager becomes entangled with the abolitionist John Brown before the American Civil War.
catalogue.why: An unusual historical series that blends absurd humour with serious politics.

catalogue.title: The Serpent Queen
catalogue.synopsis: Catherine de' Medici navigates treachery and status at the French court.
catalogue.why: Witty cynical historical politics with a strong antihero at its centre.

catalogue.title: Our Flag Means Death
catalogue.synopsis: A wealthy gentleman abandons comfort to become a hilariously incompetent pirate.
catalogue.why: Ridiculous ensemble comedy that gradually develops genuine romantic heart.

catalogue.title: Ghosts (UK)
catalogue.synopsis: A young couple inherit a mansion inhabited by quarrelling ghosts.
catalogue.why: A warmer ensemble sitcom whose comic characters may land when Parks didn't.

catalogue.title: Ghosts (US)
catalogue.synopsis: A couple renovate an inn and discover the residents include centuries of ghosts.
catalogue.why: Accessible character comedy, though perhaps too formulaic for your highest tier.

catalogue.title: Extraordinary
catalogue.synopsis: A young woman is the only person she knows without a superpower.
catalogue.why: Sharp, rude character comedy using superheroes for genuinely good jokes rather than spectacle.

catalogue.title: Misfits
catalogue.synopsis: Young offenders performing community service acquire unexpected superpowers.
catalogue.why: Profane character humour with an actual supernatural serialised plot.

catalogue.title: Crazyhead
catalogue.synopsis: Two young women discover they can see demons hiding among ordinary people.
catalogue.why: British horror comedy with strong friendship chemistry and a clear plot.

catalogue.title: The Fades
catalogue.synopsis: A teenager discovers an ability to see restless spirits threatening the living.
catalogue.why: Supernatural mystery with a short, intriguing season and unsettling mythology.

catalogue.title: Being Human (UK)
catalogue.synopsis: A vampire, a werewolf and a ghost share a house while struggling to live ordinary lives.
catalogue.why: Supernatural characters with emotional stakes and genuine ongoing story, unlike pure vampire workplace comedy.

catalogue.title: Dead Set
catalogue.synopsis: A zombie outbreak traps contestants inside a British reality-TV house.
catalogue.why: Charlie Brooker's media satire meets propulsive genre horror in a short format.

catalogue.title: The Enfield Poltergeist
catalogue.synopsis: Archival audio accompanies a reconstruction of a notorious alleged haunting.
catalogue.why: Unscripted supernatural investigation, likely less attractive than strong fictional horror.

catalogue.title: The North Water
catalogue.synopsis: A disgraced surgeon joins a brutal nineteenth-century whaling expedition.
catalogue.why: An unrelentingly tense wilderness period drama with extraordinary atmosphere.

catalogue.title: Fortitude
catalogue.synopsis: Violence ruptures an apparently idyllic Arctic community and exposes hidden secrets.
catalogue.why: Isolation, unsettling science and a continuing mystery suggest a possible Hill House/Silo crossover.

catalogue.title: The Head
catalogue.synopsis: A remote polar research station becomes the scene of a mysterious killing.
catalogue.why: A contained fictional whodunnit with psychological tension rather than true crime.

catalogue.title: The Kettering Incident
catalogue.synopsis: A doctor returns to Tasmania and confronts disappearances linked to strange lights.
catalogue.why: A slow-burn atmospheric mystery with uncanny small-town worldbuilding.

catalogue.title: The Returned
catalogue.synopsis: People long dead inexplicably reappear in a quiet French mountain town.
catalogue.why: A moving, haunting supernatural mystery with fantastic atmosphere.

catalogue.title: Black Spot
catalogue.synopsis: A police chief investigates uncanny deaths in a forest-surrounded French town.
catalogue.why: An eerie ongoing mystery with a memorable sense of place.

catalogue.title: The Chalet
catalogue.synopsis: A group of friends are stranded in an Alpine village where past secrets surface.
catalogue.why: A compact French mystery with escalating paranoia and intertwined timelines.

catalogue.title: Pagan Peak
catalogue.synopsis: Detectives from Austria and Germany pursue a killer across the mountains.
catalogue.why: A very atmospheric crime mystery, but heavier on serial-killer material than your ideal.

catalogue.title: Katla
catalogue.synopsis: After a volcanic eruption, a remote Icelandic village encounters impossible returning figures.
catalogue.why: Beautiful, eerie conceptual science fiction with emotional consequences.

catalogue.title: Trapped
catalogue.synopsis: A murder in an isolated Icelandic town coincides with a brutal blizzard.
catalogue.why: Engrossing fiction with environmental atmosphere, although conventional procedural crime.

catalogue.title: Midnight Sun
catalogue.synopsis: A French investigator travels to northern Sweden after a disturbing discovery.
catalogue.why: Noir mood and regional intrigue, but procedural elements make it exploratory.

catalogue.synopsis: Passengers on a transatlantic steamship encounter inexplicable events after meeting another vessel.
catalogue.why: Dense atmospheric conspiracy and an unusual setting; note that it was cancelled early.

catalogue.title: The Lazarus Project
catalogue.synopsis: A man discovers a secret organisation that rewinds time to prevent extinction events.
catalogue.why: Twisty plotting, morally messy characters and escalating time-loop consequences.

catalogue.title: Beforeigners
catalogue.synopsis: People from historical eras mysteriously appear in modern Oslo and struggle to assimilate.
catalogue.why: A funny, clever time-displacement premise with social satire and an ongoing mystery.

catalogue.title: The Ministry of Time
catalogue.synopsis: Spanish agents travel through history to prevent changes to the country's past.
catalogue.why: Inventive historical time-travel adventures with playful genre mechanics.

catalogue.title: The Peripheral
catalogue.synopsis: A gamer in near-future Appalachia discovers a simulated world with dangerous real consequences.
catalogue.why: Layered technology conspiracies and worldbuilding; beware its unresolved cancellation.

catalogue.title: Tales from the Loop
catalogue.synopsis: Ordinary townspeople experience strange phenomena around a mysterious research facility.
catalogue.why: Melancholy high-concept vignettes that pair ideas with quiet emotional resonance.

catalogue.title: The Lost Room
catalogue.synopsis: A detective discovers objects from an impossible motel room with extraordinary powers.
catalogue.why: A wonderfully inventive miniseries mystery that rewards attention to its rules.

catalogue.title: The Booth at the End
catalogue.synopsis: A mysterious diner patron grants wishes in exchange for difficult human tasks.
catalogue.why: Minimalist, dialogue-driven moral puzzles with a compelling conceptual hook.

catalogue.title: The Prisoner
catalogue.synopsis: A former agent is imprisoned in a surreal seaside village where his identity is attacked.
catalogue.why: An enormously influential paranoid mystery worth encountering as a television landmark.

catalogue.title: Twin Peaks
catalogue.synopsis: An FBI agent investigates a small-town murder and uncovers a bizarre hidden world.
catalogue.why: Groundbreaking mystery and surreal comedy, though its dream logic may challenge your need for payoff.

catalogue.title: Twin Peaks: The Return
catalogue.synopsis: Decades after strange events in Twin Peaks, old and new lives intertwine across impossible realities.
catalogue.why: A daring experimental TV landmark best watched after the earlier series.

catalogue.title: The X-Files
catalogue.synopsis: Two FBI agents investigate unexplained cases while a larger conspiracy emerges.
catalogue.why: A foundational supernatural mystery series combining brilliant standalone episodes and continuing mythology.

catalogue.title: Fringe
catalogue.synopsis: A scientist, his estranged son and an FBI agent uncover strange phenomena and parallel worlds.
catalogue.why: A satisfying long-running mystery that gradually builds its own ambitious mythology.

catalogue.title: Person of Interest
catalogue.synopsis: A reclusive billionaire and former agent use predictive surveillance to prevent violent crimes.
catalogue.why: Begins procedural but develops an excellent long-form AI conspiracy story.

catalogue.title: 12 Monkeys
catalogue.synopsis: A time traveller tries to stop a plague and encounters tangled causal loops.
catalogue.why: An intricate ongoing sci-fi plot with surprisingly strong emotional resolution.

catalogue.title: Travelers
catalogue.synopsis: Agents from the future inhabit present-day people to prevent catastrophe.
catalogue.why: High-concept missions alongside real emotional relationships and a continuing arc.

catalogue.title: Continuum
catalogue.synopsis: A cop from a corporate-controlled future pursues rebels into present-day Vancouver.
catalogue.why: Institutional technology intrigue and evolving questions of loyalty and freedom.

catalogue.title: Orphan Black
catalogue.synopsis: A woman discovers she has genetically identical counterparts with dangerous secrets.
catalogue.why: Propulsive identity mysteries and an extraordinary central performance.

catalogue.title: Humans
catalogue.synopsis: Lifelike household robots begin to develop independence and disrupt society.
catalogue.why: Thoughtful speculative technology with strong domestic and ethical stakes.

catalogue.title: The Capture
catalogue.synopsis: A soldier discovers surveillance footage can be manipulated as he battles a serious allegation.
catalogue.why: Topical tech-paranoia thriller with twists and institutional intrigue.

catalogue.title: State of Play
catalogue.synopsis: Journalists investigate a murder linked to an ambitious British politician.
catalogue.why: Terrific British political conspiracy writing and gripping plot, perfect for your Thick of It/Chernobyl overlap.

catalogue.title: The Honourable Woman
catalogue.synopsis: An Anglo-Israeli businesswoman becomes embroiled in dangerous diplomatic machinations.
catalogue.why: Complicated international political thriller with rich moral ambiguity.

catalogue.title: The Night Manager
catalogue.synopsis: A hotel manager infiltrates an international arms dealer's inner circle.
catalogue.why: Glossy, elegantly plotted spy intrigue with memorable characters.

catalogue.title: The Little Drummer Girl
catalogue.synopsis: A British actress is recruited into an intricate espionage operation in the Middle East.
catalogue.why: Stylish slow-burning psychological spy drama with strong period detail.

catalogue.title: Perpetual Grace, LTD
catalogue.synopsis: A grifter tries to fleece a pastor and finds himself trapped in a bizarre criminal scheme.
catalogue.why: From the Patriot creative family: eccentric noir, oddball humour and dark twists.

catalogue.title: Get Shorty
catalogue.synopsis: A mob enforcer tries to reinvent himself as a Hollywood film producer.
catalogue.why: Sharp crime-comedy absurdity with genuinely compelling characters and plot.

catalogue.title: Banshee
catalogue.synopsis: An ex-con impersonates a small-town sheriff while navigating violent local factions.
catalogue.why: Enormously entertaining pulp with a ridiculous premise and nonstop momentum.

catalogue.title: Gangs of London
catalogue.synopsis: The murder of a crime-family patriarch triggers violent struggles for control.
catalogue.why: Highly kinetic fictional underworld storytelling, more spectacle-heavy than your average favourite.

catalogue.title: ZeroZeroZero
catalogue.synopsis: A global cocaine shipment connects criminal networks, brokers and desperate families.
catalogue.why: A very cinematic thriller about systems, power and morally compromised people.

catalogue.title: Top Boy
catalogue.synopsis: Rival drug dealers and local families navigate life in an East London estate.
catalogue.why: Excellent character drama with complicated loyalties and serious social stakes.

catalogue.title: Kin
catalogue.synopsis: A Dublin crime family faces a powerful rival after a killing.
catalogue.why: Irish family loyalty and gritty narrative escalation for your darker evenings.

catalogue.title: Love/Hate
catalogue.synopsis: A Dublin criminal crew navigates escalating violence and betrayals.
catalogue.why: Hard-edged fictional crime with strong character momentum and Irish dialogue.

catalogue.title: The Responder
catalogue.synopsis: A troubled Liverpool police officer attempts to survive punishing night shifts.
catalogue.why: Intensely flawed characters and dark British humour alongside gritty drama.

catalogue.title: Time
catalogue.synopsis: An inexperienced prisoner and a conflicted guard confront a harsh correctional system.
catalogue.why: Institutional drama with devastating character stakes, an excellent Chernobyl-like character piece.

catalogue.title: The Virtues
catalogue.synopsis: A troubled man travels to Ireland to confront memories of a traumatic childhood.
catalogue.why: Raw, powerful emotional storytelling for serious evenings.

catalogue.title: This Is England '86
catalogue.synopsis: Friends in a Midlands town navigate adulthood and trauma after the original film.
catalogue.why: A landmark of working-class character storytelling with humour and heartbreak.

catalogue.title: This Is England '88
catalogue.synopsis: The same group of young adults faces painful personal decisions over Christmas.
catalogue.why: Intimate continuation with devastating emotion, best seen in order.

catalogue.title: This Is England '90
catalogue.synopsis: Old friends reunite during a turbulent summer of music and life changes.
catalogue.why: An emotionally satisfying culmination of a great British ensemble story.

catalogue.title: The Gallows Pole
catalogue.synopsis: Yorkshire workers begin a coin-forging enterprise in the eighteenth century.
catalogue.why: A very unusual historical voice and local texture, though deliberately unconventional.

catalogue.title: Happy Valley
catalogue.synopsis: A Yorkshire police sergeant confronts her family's trauma amid a criminal investigation.
catalogue.why: Outstanding character writing and emotional intensity, but crime-heavy.

catalogue.title: The English
catalogue.synopsis: An Englishwoman crosses the American West in search of revenge and unexpected companionship.
catalogue.why: Beautifully composed, emotionally powerful character adventure with a strong mystery.

catalogue.title: Godless
catalogue.synopsis: A fugitive from an outlaw gang finds refuge in a New Mexico mining town.
catalogue.why: A richly drawn, atmospheric western miniseries with exciting narrative stakes.

catalogue.synopsis: A family joins a dangerous wagon journey across the American frontier.
catalogue.why: Expansive wilderness adventure and family emotion for your Into the Wild side.

catalogue.title: Sweet Tooth
catalogue.synopsis: A sheltered half-deer boy journeys through a changed world searching for answers.
catalogue.why: An imaginative post-apocalyptic adventure with unusually sincere optimism.

catalogue.title: The Last Man on Earth
catalogue.synopsis: A self-centred survivor wanders a seemingly empty world after a pandemic.
catalogue.why: Awful characters and high-concept comic premise; its lead can be deliberately irritating.

catalogue.title: People of Earth
catalogue.synopsis: Members of a support group for alien abductees investigate their strange shared experiences.
catalogue.why: Gentle but properly quirky sitcom with a developing speculative mythology.

catalogue.title: Resident Alien
catalogue.synopsis: An extraterrestrial hiding in a Colorado town gets entangled in a murder investigation.
catalogue.why: A strong lead performance, daft small-town interactions and an actual sci-fi plot.

catalogue.title: BrainDead
catalogue.synopsis: Alien insects infect politicians and worsen Washington's already absurd dysfunction.
catalogue.why: The Thick of It meets a bizarre extraterrestrial conspiracy, with real satirical teeth.

catalogue.title: Avenue 5
catalogue.synopsis: A luxury space cruise goes catastrophically wrong under incompetent leadership.
catalogue.why: Armando Iannucci's institutional stupidity deployed in space; very plausible for you.

catalogue.title: Space Force
catalogue.synopsis: A military commander is appointed to run a new space branch with disastrous results.
catalogue.why: A mainstream workplace comedy that may be too conventional given your Superstore reaction.

catalogue.title: The Orville
catalogue.synopsis: A dysfunctional starship crew explores the galaxy and tackles unusual moral dilemmas.
catalogue.why: A surprisingly thoughtful sci-fi series hidden inside accessible ensemble humour.

catalogue.title: Lower Decks
catalogue.synopsis: Junior Starfleet officers navigate mundane and bizarre adventures aboard an overlooked ship.
catalogue.why: Genuine sci-fi creativity with fast jokes and absurd characters.

catalogue.title: Futurama
catalogue.synopsis: A delivery boy accidentally awakens in the far future and joins an eccentric spaceship crew.
catalogue.why: Brilliant sci-fi concepts, joke density and occasionally extraordinary emotional episodes.

catalogue.title: Rick and Morty
catalogue.synopsis: An irresponsible scientist drags his anxious grandson across a chaotic multiverse.
catalogue.why: Ingenious science fiction and often brutal absurd comedy, although deliberately cynical.

catalogue.title: Solar Opposites
catalogue.synopsis: An alien family struggles to survive suburban Earth with disastrous side projects.
catalogue.why: Wild genre inventiveness, but more abrasive than your safest comedy favourites.

catalogue.title: Smiling Friends
catalogue.synopsis: Employees of a tiny charity attempt to make miserable strangers smile.
catalogue.why: Short, deeply weird and intensely committed sketch-like comedy, near your ITYSL preferences.

catalogue.title: The Midnight Gospel
catalogue.synopsis: A spacecaster interviews strange beings while travelling through impossible worlds.
catalogue.why: Psychedelic animated ideas and philosophical talk; intriguing but potentially too discursive.

catalogue.title: Undone
catalogue.synopsis: A woman develops a strange ability to revisit time after surviving a crash.
catalogue.why: Inventive rotoscoped storytelling and serious emotional mysteries, ideal Maniac territory.

catalogue.title: Pantheon
catalogue.synopsis: A teenager receives messages apparently from her deceased father's uploaded consciousness.
catalogue.why: Intellectually ambitious technology thriller with family emotion and a strong continuing plot.

catalogue.title: Primal
catalogue.synopsis: A caveman and dinosaur forge a bond while surviving violent prehistoric dangers.
catalogue.why: Almost wordless action fused with unexpectedly immense emotion and imagination.

catalogue.title: Infinity Train
catalogue.synopsis: Passengers trapped aboard an endless train navigate impossible carriages reflecting personal struggles.
catalogue.why: High-concept episodic imagination with a deeper emotional mystery.

catalogue.title: Over the Garden Wall
catalogue.synopsis: Two brothers wander through a strange woodland seeking a route home.
catalogue.why: Short, funny, haunting and surprisingly moving autumnal fantasy.

catalogue.title: Bee and PuppyCat
catalogue.synopsis: An unemployed woman takes magical temporary jobs with a mysterious animal companion.
catalogue.why: Dreamy, absurd comfort watching with delightful oddball imagination.

catalogue.title: Hilda
catalogue.synopsis: A curious girl explores a world of magical creatures and mysterious local folklore.
catalogue.why: Unusually imaginative, kind-hearted animated adventure with a distinct sense of wonder.

catalogue.title: Adventure Time
catalogue.synopsis: A boy and a shape-shifting dog adventure through a wildly imaginative post-apocalyptic land.
catalogue.why: Enormous creative invention, ridiculous humour and unexpected emotional depth over time.

catalogue.title: Gravity Falls
catalogue.synopsis: Twins spending summer with an eccentric uncle uncover supernatural mysteries in a tourist town.
catalogue.why: A satisfying long-form mystery disguised as a brilliantly funny animated adventure.

catalogue.title: Amphibia
catalogue.synopsis: A teenage girl becomes stranded in a world of talking amphibians and slowly finds a new family.
catalogue.why: Big imaginative worldbuilding that grows into emotionally satisfying adventure.

catalogue.title: The Owl House
catalogue.synopsis: A human girl trains as a witch in a wonderfully strange magical realm.
catalogue.why: Oddball characters and meaningful long-form relationships with real inventive ambition.

catalogue.title: Steven Universe
catalogue.synopsis: A boy and his magical guardians defend Earth and uncover a complicated history.
catalogue.why: Big-hearted emotional storytelling that develops a surprisingly rich mythology.

catalogue.title: The Legend of Vox Machina
catalogue.synopsis: A gang of misfit adventurers confront dangerous forces while arguing constantly.
catalogue.why: Rude ensemble humour and a proper fantasy quest with emotional growth.

catalogue.title: Harley Quinn
catalogue.synopsis: A newly independent antihero tries to make it in Gotham's criminal underworld.
catalogue.why: A brilliantly profane comic-book sitcom that values jokes and character over formulaic superhero action.

catalogue.title: Doom Patrol
catalogue.synopsis: A traumatised team of superpowered outsiders confronts increasingly absurd threats.
catalogue.why: One of the weirdest and most heartfelt comic-book shows, with distinctive character writing.

catalogue.title: Legion
catalogue.synopsis: A troubled mutant questions his own mind while navigating a surreal struggle for power.
catalogue.why: Radical visual imagination and an ambitious psychological mystery beyond superhero conventions.

catalogue.title: Watchmen
catalogue.synopsis: A masked detective uncovers a conspiracy in an alternate-history Tulsa.
catalogue.why: Superhero mythology used for sharp social commentary and an intricate ongoing mystery.

catalogue.title: WandaVision
catalogue.synopsis: Two Avengers inhabit an idyllic television sitcom world that slowly reveals unsettling secrets.
catalogue.why: One of Marvel's strongest high-concept mysteries with a genuine emotional core.

catalogue.title: Moon Knight
catalogue.synopsis: A museum worker discovers other identities and becomes entwined with Egyptian gods.
catalogue.why: Psychological identity mystery gives the action something more interesting to do.

catalogue.title: Werewolf by Night
catalogue.synopsis: Monster hunters gather for a secret contest with chilling consequences.
catalogue.why: An unusually stylish, concise Marvel horror experiment instead of generic superhero spectacle.

catalogue.title: Echo
catalogue.synopsis: A former criminal enforcer returns home and faces complicated family loyalties.
catalogue.why: A grounded Marvel character drama that prioritises identity over cosmic spectacle.

catalogue.title: Jessica Jones
catalogue.synopsis: A hard-drinking investigator confronts an abuser with mind-control powers.
catalogue.why: A compelling psychological crime story with morally messy characters, beyond conventional action.

catalogue.title: Daredevil
catalogue.synopsis: A blind lawyer secretly fights organised crime on New York's streets.
catalogue.why: Compelling villains, moral conflict and sustained drama over franchise spectacle.

catalogue.title: The Mandalorian
catalogue.synopsis: A lone bounty hunter protects a mysterious child while travelling the galaxy.
catalogue.why: Warm adventure and character chemistry, better for your escapist than cerebral mood.

catalogue.title: Ahsoka
catalogue.synopsis: A former Jedi investigates a potential threat emerging after the Empire's defeat.
catalogue.why: An adventure with mythology and connections, but less standalone intrigue than Andor.

catalogue.title: Firefly
catalogue.synopsis: The misfit crew of a smuggling spaceship scrapes together jobs on a dangerous frontier.
catalogue.why: Fantastic ensemble banter, worldbuilding and characters worth caring about.

catalogue.title: Battlestar Galactica
catalogue.synopsis: The last human survivors flee a robotic enemy while facing political and moral fractures.
catalogue.why: An influential serialised sci-fi drama with strong institutions, stakes and mystery.

catalogue.title: Foundation
catalogue.synopsis: Scientists and dynasties struggle over predictions about a collapsing galactic empire.
catalogue.why: Grand ambition, imperial politics and imaginative future history, though sprawling.

catalogue.title: Raised by Wolves
catalogue.synopsis: Two androids raise human children on a hostile alien planet amid religious conflict.
catalogue.why: Extraordinarily odd worldbuilding and philosophical intrigue, but unresolved cancellation.

catalogue.title: The First
catalogue.synopsis: An American space programme prepares a dangerous crewed Mars mission.
catalogue.why: Reflective character-driven near-future sci-fi for serious space enthusiasts.

catalogue.title: Away
catalogue.synopsis: An astronaut leads the first Mars mission while family troubles continue on Earth.
catalogue.why: Accessible emotional space adventure, though less original than your strongest sci-fi favourites.

catalogue.title: Night Sky
catalogue.synopsis: An elderly couple secretly guards a portal to an apparently deserted planet.
catalogue.why: A lovely speculative hook and touching characters, though cancelled after one season.

catalogue.title: Outer Range
catalogue.synopsis: A Wyoming rancher discovers an impossible void on his property amid family disputes.
catalogue.why: Rural mystery, science fiction and complex family tension with unusual atmosphere.

catalogue.title: The Society
catalogue.synopsis: Teenagers return to an emptied version of their hometown and form a new government.
catalogue.why: An engaging isolation mystery whose cancellation leaves major questions open.

catalogue.title: The 4400
catalogue.synopsis: Thousands of missing people reappear together with unusual abilities.
catalogue.why: Compelling serialised mystery about unexplained returns and their social consequences.

catalogue.title: The 100
catalogue.synopsis: Young survivors are sent to a supposedly uninhabitable Earth after a nuclear catastrophe.
catalogue.why: Starts as young-adult adventure, then develops more ambitious moral dilemmas.

catalogue.title: The Last Ship
catalogue.synopsis: A naval destroyer becomes central to humanity's response to a global pandemic.
catalogue.why: A propulsive speculative adventure, more straightforward than cerebral.

catalogue.title: Electric Dreams
catalogue.synopsis: Individual stories adapt Philip K. Dick's speculative visions of reality and identity.
catalogue.why: Anthology sci-fi with varied imaginative hooks; useful beyond Black Mirror.

catalogue.title: Dimension 404
catalogue.synopsis: Different stand-alone stories explore bizarre technology and alternate realities.
catalogue.why: A lighter, inconsistent but occasionally inventive cousin to Black Mirror.

catalogue.title: Room 104
catalogue.synopsis: Different guests experience comedy, horror and strange events in the same motel room.
catalogue.why: An experimental anthology that gives you plenty of short-form creative risks.

catalogue.title: Calls
catalogue.synopsis: A series of mysterious phone calls reveals catastrophes through sound and minimal visuals.
catalogue.why: A radically concise science-fiction mystery perfect for concentrated short viewing.

catalogue.title: The Twilight Zone
catalogue.synopsis: Ordinary people encounter uncanny reversals and speculative moral puzzles.
catalogue.why: The foundational anthology series behind much of the Black Mirror tradition.

catalogue.title: Alfred Hitchcock Presents
catalogue.synopsis: A host introduces short suspense stories often ending in macabre irony.
catalogue.why: Sharp compact plot reversals and institutional irony, though dated in pacing.

catalogue.title: Tales from the Crypt
catalogue.synopsis: A wisecracking crypt-keeper introduces lurid, twisted morality tales.
catalogue.why: Nasty black humour and entertaining supernatural comeuppance for lighter horror nights.

catalogue.title: Creepshow
catalogue.synopsis: Different short stories bring campy comic-book horror to life.
catalogue.why: Unashamedly pulpy horror entertainment with some wonderfully nasty jokes.

catalogue.title: Guillermo del Toro's Cabinet of Curiosities
catalogue.synopsis: Different filmmakers tell lavishly realised tales of supernatural terror.
catalogue.why: A well-crafted way to sample atmospheres and concepts without long commitments.

catalogue.title: Channel Zero
catalogue.synopsis: Each season turns an unsettling internet legend into a distinctive supernatural nightmare.
catalogue.why: Inventive, unnerving horror mysteries with strong standalone seasonal structures.

catalogue.title: Evil
catalogue.synopsis: A sceptical psychologist joins a team investigating apparent demonic possessions.
catalogue.why: A surprisingly smart procedural that balances psychological mysteries, humour and serialised mythology.

catalogue.title: Servant
catalogue.synopsis: A grieving couple hires a mysterious nanny and unsettling events engulf their townhouse.
catalogue.why: Claustrophobic psychological horror with a developing family mystery.

catalogue.title: The Haunting of Bly Manor
catalogue.synopsis: A governess arrives at an English manor with a complicated supernatural history.
catalogue.why: Another Flanagan ghost story with emotional weight, though more romantic than Hill House.

catalogue.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
catalogue.synopsis: A corrupt family's heirs die as their patriarch recounts a lifetime of wrongdoing.
catalogue.why: Mike Flanagan's nastiest blend of dynastic satire, gothic horror and family secrets.

catalogue.title: Marianne
catalogue.synopsis: A horror novelist returns to her hometown as the monster from her books becomes real.
catalogue.why: A particularly frightening French supernatural mystery with a strong hook.

catalogue.title: Ju-On: Origins
catalogue.synopsis: A researcher investigates a haunted house linked to generations of tragedy.
catalogue.why: Extremely bleak Japanese horror mythology, not casual Sunday viewing.

catalogue.title: Paranormal
catalogue.synopsis: An Egyptian haematologist faces events that challenge his lifelong scepticism.
catalogue.why: Interesting period folklore and supernatural investigations with an unusual setting.

catalogue.title: Kingdom
catalogue.synopsis: A Korean prince investigates a plague that turns the dead into monsters.
catalogue.why: Brilliantly propulsive political intrigue and zombie horror with strong storytelling.

catalogue.title: Hellbound
catalogue.synopsis: Supernatural predictions of death trigger religious panic and new forms of authority.
catalogue.why: Institutional satire and unsettling speculative horror in an ambitious series.

catalogue.title: Sweet Home
catalogue.synopsis: Apartment residents fight to survive as people transform into monsters.
catalogue.why: Emotionally charged survival horror, somewhat more action-driven than your highest preferences.

catalogue.title: Alice in Borderland
catalogue.synopsis: Friends enter a deserted Tokyo and must survive increasingly elaborate deadly games.
catalogue.why: Addictive mystery-worldbuilding and rule-based puzzles alongside character stakes.

catalogue.title: The 8 Show
