catalogue.synopsis: Eight participants enter a peculiar money-making game governed by cruel incentives.
catalogue.why: Squid Game-style structures with pointed social satire and morally terrible decisions.

catalogue.title: Squid Game
catalogue.synopsis: Debt-ridden contestants compete in deadly versions of childhood games.
catalogue.why: A compelling thriller powered by vicious satire of institutions and inequality.

catalogue.title: The Silent Sea
catalogue.synopsis: Scientists investigating an abandoned lunar base confront a deadly secret.
catalogue.why: Space survival mystery and eerie atmosphere in a manageable limited run.

catalogue.title: The School Nurse Files
catalogue.synopsis: A school nurse fights invisible supernatural creatures affecting students.
catalogue.why: An exceptionally odd and playful Korean genre experiment.

catalogue.title: Moving
catalogue.synopsis: Teenagers with inherited abilities uncover dangerous secrets about their parents.
catalogue.why: A superhero story unusually focused on emotional family stakes and a proper conspiracy.

catalogue.title: Extraordinary Attorney Woo
catalogue.synopsis: An autistic rookie lawyer finds her feet at a prestigious legal firm.
catalogue.why: Warm relationships and clever episodic legal situations with humour.

catalogue.title: Reply 1988
catalogue.synopsis: Families and friends grow together in a tight-knit Seoul neighbourhood in the late 1980s.
catalogue.why: An exceptionally moving ensemble whose warmth is earned through everyday character writing.

catalogue.title: Hospital Playlist
catalogue.synopsis: Five longtime friends balance medical careers and their shared love of music.
catalogue.why: Genuinely affectionate ensemble drama with satisfying comedy and relationships.

catalogue.title: My Mister
catalogue.synopsis: A struggling young woman and exhausted engineer find unexpected solidarity.
catalogue.why: A demanding but extraordinarily moving character drama about loneliness and grace.

catalogue.title: Move to Heaven
catalogue.synopsis: A young man and his uncle clean the homes of people who have died.
catalogue.why: A deeply humane, often tear-inducing story that favours empathy over sentimentality.

catalogue.title: D.P.
catalogue.synopsis: South Korean soldiers track deserters while confronting abuses in the military.
catalogue.why: Institutional critique, compelling character stakes and serious drama.

catalogue.title: The Glory
catalogue.synopsis: A woman executes a detailed revenge plan against former school tormentors.
catalogue.why: Strong, ongoing plotting and psychologically complicated vengeance.

catalogue.title: Mask Girl
catalogue.synopsis: An office worker's secret online persona drags several lives into spiralling chaos.
catalogue.why: Bold tonal shifts and vicious social satire, very much your darker wild-card territory.

catalogue.title: Bargain
catalogue.synopsis: A ruthless underground auction is disrupted by an earthquake, trapping everyone.
catalogue.why: An incredibly nasty high-concept thriller with sustained escalation.

catalogue.title: A Shop for Killers
catalogue.synopsis: A young woman discovers her uncle's secret legacy as highly trained killers pursue her.
catalogue.why: Very entertaining action tied to a steadily unfolding family mystery.

catalogue.title: Pachinko
catalogue.synopsis: Generations of a Korean family navigate displacement, discrimination and love.
catalogue.why: A gorgeous, deeply emotional multigenerational epic.

catalogue.title: Shōgun
catalogue.synopsis: An English sailor becomes a pawn in rivalries among powerful Japanese lords.
catalogue.why: Rich political manoeuvring, character psychology and stunning historical worldbuilding.

catalogue.title: The Sympathizer
catalogue.synopsis: A North Vietnamese spy navigates exile and shifting loyalties after the Vietnam War.
catalogue.why: An audacious political satire and identity thriller with unusual comic bite.

catalogue.title: Tokyo Vice
catalogue.synopsis: An American reporter enters Tokyo's dangerous criminal and journalistic worlds.
catalogue.why: Strong atmosphere, institution-focused plotting and morally complex people.

catalogue.title: Giri/Haji
catalogue.synopsis: A Tokyo detective searches London for his fugitive brother while confronting criminal loyalties.
catalogue.why: Stylish, sometimes funny cross-cultural noir with excellent character relationships.

catalogue.title: The Makanai: Cooking for the Maiko House
catalogue.synopsis: Two teenage friends pursue different lives in a traditional Kyoto apprentice house.
catalogue.why: Gentle food and friendship storytelling for genuinely relaxing evenings.

catalogue.title: Midnight Diner
catalogue.synopsis: Late-night Tokyo customers share their stories over simple meals.
catalogue.why: Quiet, human little tales with understated humour and warmth.

catalogue.title: Samurai Gourmet
catalogue.synopsis: A newly retired man discovers everyday dining through fantasies of a wandering samurai.
catalogue.why: A delightfully specific low-stakes comedy for meals and quiet nights.

catalogue.title: Old Enough!
catalogue.synopsis: Very young children attempt simple errands while hidden cameras observe.
catalogue.why: Tiny everyday adventures with charming surprises, extremely low commitment.

catalogue.title: Joe Pera Talks with You
catalogue.synopsis: A soft-spoken Michigan choir teacher shares gentle reflections on ordinary subjects.
catalogue.why: A distinctive, profoundly calming and occasionally moving alternative to conventional comfort sitcoms.

catalogue.title: Documentary Now!
catalogue.synopsis: Comedians meticulously parody different documentary filmmaking styles.
catalogue.why: Deeply committed genre parody and performers taking ridiculous ideas seriously.

catalogue.title: The Eric Andre Show
catalogue.synopsis: A fake talk show repeatedly dissolves into aggressively surreal chaos.
catalogue.why: An extreme test of your love for committed weird sketch comedy.

catalogue.title: Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!
catalogue.synopsis: Lo-fi public-access television aesthetics become aggressively bizarre sketches.
catalogue.why: Foundational deliberately awful-looking absurdism, a possible ITYSL ancestor.

catalogue.title: The Birthday Boys
catalogue.synopsis: An ensemble stages silly, surreal sketches with escalating premises.
catalogue.why: Deep-cut American absurd sketch work that could scratch your ITYSL itch.

catalogue.title: Aunty Donna's Big Ol' House of Fun
catalogue.synopsis: Three Australian comedians turn mundane household life into impossible musical chaos.
catalogue.why: Superbly committed, high-energy absurdism where every bit goes somewhere ridiculous.

catalogue.title: The Characters
catalogue.synopsis: Comedians are each given a complete episode to construct eccentric sketches.
catalogue.why: A chance to discover exceptionally idiosyncratic performers and stranger joke structures.

catalogue.title: Comedy Bang! Bang!
catalogue.synopsis: A mock talk show combines deadpan interviews and increasingly absurd interruptions.
catalogue.why: Improv-driven surreal comedy with many inventive guest characters.

catalogue.title: Jury Duty
catalogue.synopsis: An unsuspecting juror serves on a mock trial secretly populated by actors.
catalogue.why: An ingenious prank format with warmth and meticulously constructed comic situations.

catalogue.title: The Joe Schmo Show
catalogue.synopsis: One unsuspecting participant joins what seems to be a reality show staffed by actors.
catalogue.why: A fascinating early social-comedy construction with unpredictable emotional moments.

catalogue.title: Taskmaster (NZ)
catalogue.synopsis: New Zealand comedians attempt absurd assignments under a stern host and assistant.
catalogue.why: Very natural extension of your enjoyment of Taskmaster, with some superbly silly performers.

catalogue.title: Game Changer
catalogue.synopsis: Comedians enter a game show without knowing the rules until the challenge begins.
catalogue.why: Genuinely inventive comic structures and ridiculous improvisation, a strong hidden find.

catalogue.title: Make Some Noise
catalogue.synopsis: Performers race to improvise voices, scenes and absurd prompts.
catalogue.why: High-density quick comedy with outstanding improvisers for switch-off evenings.

catalogue.title: Would I Lie to You?
catalogue.synopsis: Panellists try to distinguish outrageous true stories from entirely invented ones.
catalogue.why: Brilliant character banter and escalating absurd anecdotes with almost no viewing commitment.

catalogue.title: The Last Leg
catalogue.synopsis: Comedians discuss news and current events with an irreverent tone.
catalogue.why: Personality-led commentary for casual evenings, though topical quality varies.

catalogue.title: 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown
catalogue.synopsis: Comedians battle through a deliberately ridiculous version of the word-and-number game.
catalogue.why: Banter, absurd personalities and effortless standalone entertainment.

catalogue.title: The Big Fat Quiz of the Year
catalogue.synopsis: Comedian teams compete in a comic retrospective of a year's events.
catalogue.why: Excellent easy-watch banter and long-form ridiculousness rather than narrative commitment.

catalogue.title: QI
catalogue.synopsis: Panellists explore surprising facts while dodging obvious but incorrect answers.
catalogue.why: A clever alternative to scripted comedy when your mood is light and curious.

catalogue.title: Travel Man
catalogue.synopsis: A comedian and a celebrity companion explore a destination on an absurdly tight schedule.
catalogue.why: Personality-led travel with dry banter, a natural Top Gear crossover.

catalogue.title: The Trip
catalogue.synopsis: Two comedians review restaurants in northern England while competing at impressions.
catalogue.why: Improvised travel banter for the Grand Tour-loving part of your taste.

catalogue.title: The Reluctant Traveler
catalogue.synopsis: Eugene Levy explores different destinations despite his many travel anxieties.
catalogue.why: A personality-driven travel series with charming comedy and beautiful locations.

catalogue.title: An Idiot Abroad
catalogue.synopsis: Karl Pilkington reluctantly travels to extraordinary locations under mischievous supervision.
catalogue.why: Excellent personality-based absurdity and travel, very much in your old Top Gear lane.

catalogue.title: The Moaning of Life
catalogue.synopsis: Karl Pilkington investigates life's big questions through baffling world experiences.
catalogue.why: Travel, dry comedy and striking cultural situations without required narrative commitment.

catalogue.title: James May: Our Man in Japan
catalogue.synopsis: James May travels the length of Japan exploring traditions and everyday life.
catalogue.why: Exactly the curiosity and dry personality banter you liked about old Top Gear.

catalogue.title: James May: Our Man in Italy
catalogue.synopsis: James May crosses Italy exploring history, industry and food.
catalogue.why: Gentle travel comedy powered by a personality you're already predisposed to enjoy.

catalogue.title: Clarkson's Farm
catalogue.synopsis: Jeremy Clarkson tries to run an English farm despite almost complete inexperience.
catalogue.why: Top Gear personality chaos blended with genuine connection to farming and people.

catalogue.title: Richard Hammond's Workshop
catalogue.synopsis: Richard Hammond tries to establish a classic-car restoration business.
catalogue.why: A familiar personality navigating tangible real-world problems and workshop banter.
